title: St. Ursula's Penelope Bolinger wins Bengals Flag Football Player of the Year
description: The Bengals named their 2026 Girls Flag Football Player of the Year during their preseason opener on Aug. 13. Here's what to know about the star QB.
fullText:
After leading the Bulldogs to their first state championship appearance, St. Ursula quarterback Penelope Bolinger has been named the 2026 Bengals Girls Flag Football Player of the Year.

The Cincinnati Bengals honored Bolinger in a ceremony during halftime of their preseason opener on Aug. 13, 2026. She was surprised with a personalized Bengals jersey to commemorate the accomplishment. Bolinger was joined by the rest of the Bulldogs flag football team to celebrate.

Bolinger, a 2026 St. Ursula graduate, was one of the top quarterbacks in the state last season. She finished the year ranked No. 1 in Ohio by MaxPreps with 312 completions for 3,394 passing yards and 61 touchdowns. St. Ursula's team captain was also named to the Enquirer's all-city first team. The Bulldogs finished as runners-up in the Cincinnati regional tournament at Paycor Stadium, earning a trip to the Ohio High School Athletic Association's first sanctioned tournament.

Bolinger was a dedicated multisport athlete and leader at St. Ursula. She helped the Bulldogs win the Division II state volleyball title in 2024 and committed to continue her volleyball career at Wittenberg University. Bolinger volunteered over 25 hours at youth flag football camps, mentoring fifth through eighth grade athletes and helping grow the nascent sport. She also graduated with a 3.8 GPA.

After the award presentation, Bolinger took the field one final time as St. Ursula competed against Mount Notre Dame and Badin during halftime. The exhibitions are part of the Bengals commitment to growing the sport; the NFL franchise also provides local schools with equipment and training and hosts the annual regional tournament at Paycor Stadium.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: St. Ursula's Penelope Bolinger wins Bengals Flag Football Player of the Year

title: Chris Paul Could Reportedly Join Lakers’ Front Office
description: Chris Paul never played for the Lakers, but his relationship with incoming owner Bob Iger could finally bring him to the franchise in a powerful new role.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers could add one of the NBA's most respected basketball minds to their front office following the franchise's record-setting sale.

Recently retired point guard Chris Paul could eventually have a role with the Lakers because of his close relationship with incoming owner Bob Iger, according to ESPN's Dave McMenamin.

"Multiple sources around the league suggested to ESPN that the recently retired Chris Paul could have a role," McMenamin wrote.

McMenamin: Chris Paul "could have a role" in Lakers' front office after sale due to his close relationship with Bob Iger.

Paul and Iger reportedly became close while Paul played for the Clippers and Iger held season tickets. No formal position or agreement has been reported, making Paul's possible involvement something to monitor rather than a confirmed addition.

Paul retired after 21 NBA seasons as one of the most accomplished point guards in league history. The 12-time All-Star also earned 11 All-NBA selections and nine All-Defensive selections while establishing himself as a respected leader across the league.

His experience extends beyond what he accomplished on the court. Paul served as president of the National Basketball Players Association from 2013 to 2021, representing players during negotiations with team owners and league officials.

That background could make him an intriguing candidate for a basketball operations, player relations or advisory position. Paul understands roster construction from a player's perspective and has built relationships with stars, executives and agents throughout his career.

His arrival would also add a new voice to a Lakers organization entering a dramatically different era.

Paul has been connected to the Lakers for more than a decade, although he never played for the franchise.

In December 2011, the Lakers agreed to acquire Paul from the New Orleans Hornets in a three-team trade involving the Houston Rockets. The deal was blocked by then-NBA commissioner David Stern, who was acting on behalf of the league-owned Hornets.

Paul was traded to the Clippers days later and helped transform L.A.'s other team into a consistent playoff contender. He remained with the Clippers for six seasons before playing for Houston, Oklahoma City, Phoenix, Golden State and San Antonio.

A potential front-office role would finally place Paul inside the Lakers organization, even if it comes long after his playing career ended.

Iger and Josh Kushner agreed to purchase the Lakers from Mark Walter for a reported $12.5 billion, a transaction that would set a record for a professional sports franchise. The sale still must complete the league's approval process.

Major ownership changes often lead to questions about organizational structure, but there has been no indication that Paul would replace president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka or immediately take control of personnel decisions.

For now, Paul represents a compelling possibility. His connection with Iger, leadership history and understanding of modern players could make him a valuable addition as the Lakers begin another major transition.

title: Kyle Larson wins Knoxville Nationals pole but is at peace he (probably) can't race
description: However, rain could change things ...
fullText:
Kyle Larson won the Thursday Knoxville Nationals preliminary night and secured the pole for the 65th running of the Grandaddy of Them All but will more than likely be unable to start the $200,000-to-win main event.

This seemed inevitable last week when the three-time winner of the world's most prestigious Sprint Car race filed an entry even though he's known for a year that the main event would take place at the same time as the NASCAR Cup Series race at Richmond on Saturday.

He's not bothered by needing to go to work this weekend because this was always the plan. The only scenario that would see him race for a fourth Nationals victory would require rain.

Hold that thought for a moment.

"I think everybody would expect me to feel that way, but I've known it all along," Larson said of his lack of disappointment. "That helps my mindset of accepting that I can't race on Saturday.

"So no, I don't feel upset or bittersweet about anything. I came here with the goal of winning the prelim night and being a high point guy, and we did that. So yeah, if anything, I think it's just fun for me to give Trevor Canales another start in the Knoxville Nationals."

That's the plan, by the way, having crew member Trevor Canales start-and-park the car from the back of the field. Its the car that qualifies into this race and not the driver. Canales' similarly start-and-parked for Rico Abreu in 2015 when he had an ARCA conflict that year while also driving for Silva.

Even though Larson is most likely missing out on Saturday, his win on Thursday paid $12,000 and finishing last in the feature effectively earned the Paul Silva owned team another $15,000. They also won the Front Row Challenge on Monday at Southern Iowa Speedway, which paid $21,000 and the Capitani Classic on Sunday, paying $13,000-to-win.

Larson drives for Silva, and that No. 57 car is a business that puts food on the table for Silva and Canales. Larson effectively is an employee who just generated a lot of business for his friend, collaborator and car owner.

"I mean, Paul and Trevor do this for a living, and I think most people think that I own this and I pay for everything, but I'm strictly a driver and I race for Paul Silva.

"So whenever I race, it's an opportunity for him to make money. So that's not the main reason why we ran the prelim night or anything like that, because it's an opportunity to race but it did pay 12 grand to win.

"And when you win that, it meant 15 grand guaranteed on top of that for starting. So yeah, that's a lot of money for a guy who does this for a living. I think anybody watching would appreciate that and take that. I understand anyone's frustrations or whatever. I haven't heard it from any of my competitors. It's just the DARFs but that's to be expected."

That's 'Dumb Ass Race Fan' for the uninitiated.

Now, there is a marginal threat of rain on Saturday at Knoxville. And it's rained all week, and while Larson wouldn't complain about the race being delayed to Sunday, he's focused on NASCAR until Richmond ends.

If that race ends and there's still a chance to fly back into Knoxville, he'll go for it. He's just not banking on it.

"I mean, if there's an opportunity for me to be here, I'm going to try to be here," Larson said. "But when I get in the Cup car, my mind is not going to be on Knoxville at all. It never is. I think that's also a misconception I feel like people think about me. But when I'm in the Cup car, that's all I think about. And right now, I mean, seeing the checkered flag ways, my mind shifts literally to like, all right, it's Richmond practice. 'What do I need to feel? Qualifying. I go out early. What do I need to do?' I just think a racer, all racers, but especially me jumping in different cars, it's like whenever this one event ends, my mind is already onto the next thing. So I'm physically in Knoxville, but I'm mentally in Richmond right now. So I need to go there and try and do a good job."

title: Whittingham says Michigan QB Bryce Underwood earns A-plus grade in camp
description: After a shaky spring, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood is earning high praise from coach Kyle Whittingham.
fullText:
Fans weren't exactly brimming with confidence after Bryce Underwood put on the winged helmet in the spring game. After going 3-for-9, the level of development at that point in the offseason was underwhelming, and fans and media alike wondered aloud: is he developing at a pace that will allow him to win games for Michigan football this season?

Given the difficult schedule, Underwood needs to take a step further beyond his up-and-down freshman campaign. He completed 60% of his passes for 2,428 yards, 392 yards rushing, with 17 touchdowns overall and nine interceptions. His 11-to-9 passing touchdowns to interception ratio left a lot to be desired, and even though that latter number swelled in the bowl game (he threw two touchdowns but also three interceptions), Michigan is going to need more from him.

So all eyes this offseason have been on Underwood, and head coach Kyle Whittingham insists he's actually coming along better than anticipated.

Speaking on the Big Ten Network's inside look into the Wolverines' fall camp, Whittingham gave Underwood a perfect grade through six practices as of Wednesday. He says he's seen the work and he's now seeing the progress on the field.

"He's coming along well," Whittingham said. "He's had a great first six days. He's much further ahead than he was at the end of spring. He obviously worked hard this summer and did a lot of positive things, getting himself ready in the film room, on the field. And so far through six practices, I graded him an A-plus."

The hope and goal is that Underwood will somewhat emulate Utah's quarterback last year, Devon Dampier. Dampier didn't throw for much more than Underwood had -- just 62 yards more -- but he rushed for nearly triple the amount, and had a TD-to-INT ratio of 24-to-5.

Whittingham says that the offense will be tailored to Underwood's skill set, and with that, they hope that he'll be that much more successful in games.

"Well, a lot of it, but the mark of a coach that knows what he's doing is he's gonna tailor things to his players," Whittingham said. "And Devon had a skill set that was what he had, and then Bryce has what he has. And so our job as coaches is to make sure we play to the strengths of especially the quarterback. And Bryce has a ton of physical ability. He's got a big-time arm. He does a lot of things well, but in the final analysis us putting him in position to succeed is what our job is. And we're trying, working hard doing that."

Fall camp will continue through the month, with eyes on the September 5 season opener against Western Michigan at The Big House.

title: World champ McIntosh crashes out of Pan Pacs 400m free
description:
World record-holder Summer McIntosh failed to qualify for the 400m freestyle final at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, California, on Friday, slumping to the ninth-quickest time in the heats.She went on to win the 400m individual medley on Thursday, shattering the championship record but saying she was disappointed in her time of 4:28.01, which was more than four seconds slower than her world mark.
bb/ea
fullText:
World record-holder Summer McIntosh failed to qualify for the 400m freestyle final at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, California, on Friday, slumping to the ninth-quickest time in the heats.

The 19-year-old Canadian sensation, who won three gold medals at the Paris Olympics, clocked 4min 08.56sec -- more than 14 seconds outside the world record she set last year before going on to win the world title in Singapore.

McIntosh had been expected to figure in a three-way battle for the Pan Pacs crown with US freestyle great Katie Ledecky and Australian Lani Pallister.

Ledecky led the way into Friday night's final with a time of 4:03.48 and Pallister, who won the 200m free and took silver behind Ledecky in the 1,500m on Wednesday, was fourth-quickest.

The competition that brings together top swimmers from non-European countries has been a mixed bag for McIntosh.

After dropping one of her signature events, the 200m butterfly, to focus on the 200m free she finished runner-up to Pallister. She went on to win the 400m individual medley on Thursday, shattering the championship record but saying she was disappointed in her time of 4:28.01, which was more than four seconds slower than her world mark.

title: Latest fallout from shocking Lakers sale: Would LeBron have stayed? Chris Paul into front office?
description: Also, how are Lakers fans feeling about all of this?
fullText:
The NBA — and Lakers fans — are still reeling from the shocking sale of the iconic franchise for the second time in 14 months this week. Nobody saw this coming, including the league office.

There's been a lot of fallout from the news of the sale, here are some of the latest reports.

That remains the $12.5 billion question, but the answer is coming more into focus:

Money. It's always about the money.

There are a lot of ideas and White House-tied conspiracy theories floating around about what motivated Walter to sell the Lakers 14 months after agreeing to purchase them, but the answer may be the most obvious one. Walter is facing twin federal and SEC investigations into potential fraud tied to the valuation of insurance companies he owns through Guggenheim Partners and TWG Global, and in the wake of that, needed cash fast to pay down debts.

Then Joshua Kushner called, and his venture capital firm Thrive had the cash (they were looking into getting an NBA expansion team in Las Vegas, plus they were the primary buyers in the now-scuttled FIFA plan to sell rights to the World Cup and other events, so they were ready to spend). It came together quickly.

One other note: Walter Mark Walter could save roughly $425 million in taxes if the Board of Governors approve the sale and it goes through by November, according to tax calculations in an article at Sportico.

LeBron James left the Lakers this offseason in an amicable divorce, as the franchise reshaped itself around Luka Doncic's playing style. Might LeBron have stayed in Los Angeles if the Lakers had different ownership? ESPN's Dave McMenamin asked that of a source close to LeBron.

"Maybe. But that's tough to answer. Communication could have been better [with Iger and Kushner, compared to with Walter]. Just a different relationship. But the basketball piece was the most important, so maybe not from that standpoint."

From my perspective, I don't think new owners would have changed anything. First, the vibe that LeBron wasn't returning was evident around the team by midway through the season — the Lakers needed to pivot to a team built around Doncic, and everyone understood that. New ownership doesn't change that.

Plus, LeBron landed in a very interesting place — with a better chance of getting another ring — in Philadelphia.

David Stern famously nixed Chris Paul being traded to the Lakers in 2011, but could the future Hall of Fame point guard have a role with the team's front office under new ownership?

It's been speculated about because CP3 and new owner Bob Iger are so close, reports ESPN's McMenamin.

...multiple sources around the league suggested to ESPN that recently retired Chris Paul could have a role. Paul and Iger became close while the point guard played for the Clippers and Iger was a season-ticket holder."

Like everyone else, Lakers fans are shocked. Part of what helped grow the Lakers into a global icon was stability — the Buss family owned and ran the team for 46 years.

Lakers fans understood the sale of the team to Walter. The era of mom-and-pop family ownership of major American sports franchises is over, it takes deeper pockets to compete. Walter had those, and had a track record of spending and success in Los Angeles with the Dodgers — and he was bringing the beefed-up scouting staff and analytics bent of the Dodgers to the Lakers.

Now? Lakers fans I have spoken to in the last 48 hours (I live in the greater Los Angeles area with a lot of Lakers fans as friends) are both shocked, and there is an air of trepidation. Walter was a known quantity, but the Kushner/Iger team has never been the primary owners of a major sports franchise. Nobody knows what their ownership style will be, what this will look like. What does this mean for Rob Pelinka as the head of basketball operations?

Magic Johnson tried to calm Lakers fans' fears.

Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners. I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years - he has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA.

It's going to take more than words — and Iger will be the one doing the talking. While Kushner is the money behind this and will be the controlling owner, Iger will be the face of ownership. It's going to be about actions. The Lakers began a needed retooling this offseason to build a team around Doncic, but this is very likely not a championship team as constructed (not in the West with two juggernauts at the top). There is a lot of pressure on Walker Kessler and Austin Reaves to live up to massive new contracts. When things go wrong, as they inevitably will on some level, how will the new ownership handle the situation?

The new owners will have to win over Lakers fans. That may take time.

title: Former Gator Bradley Beal remains with Clippers after new contract
description: After waiting throughout most of the free agency period, former Florida basketball guard Bradley Beal re-signs with the Los Angeles Clippers.
fullText:
Former Florida basketball guard Bradley Beal has agreed to a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the LA Clippers, ESPN reports. The deal includes a player option in the second season.

After declining his $5.6 million player option, Beal spent the past month exploring his options in free agency, including interest from the Miami Heat, before ultimately deciding to remain with the Clippers.

Beal's decision to opt out allowed him to test his value on the open market while also giving Los Angeles additional flexibility to explore its roster options. In the end, the Clippers opted to retain Beal with a significant raise on a new two-year contract.

Beal's first season with the Clippers did not go as planned, as he only appeared in six games, but the new contract allows him to reset heading into his 15th NBA season. Beal, a three-time NBA All-Star, will look to stay healthy and recapture the form that made him one of the league's premier scoring guards during his time with the Washington Wizards.

With Los Angeles transitioning toward a younger roster, Beal's experience could provide valuable leadership while he looks to carve out a meaningful role on the second unit. If he can return to form, the former Gator could prove to be an important piece for the Clippers over the next two seasons.

title: Report: Liverpool ready to move for 18-year-old forward

fullText:
With just a couple of weeks to go in the transfer window, Liverpool are finally ready to push hard in the market.

Jeremy Jacquet, Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo have all arrived already, but there's plenty of work to be done still.

Liverpool's priority remains PSG forward Bradley Barcola, with talks still active over a deal likely to be above £100m.

However, according to reports in France, Liverpool are ready to move for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye…

According to L'Equipe, Liverpool are set to make a concrete proposal to PSG by the end of next week.

Whilst Mbaye's price tag is likely to be above the €40m initially reported,he likely represents a cheaper option for the Reds.

Andoni Iraola's squad still has a huge Mohamed Salah-shaped hole in it, where Mbaye could be utilised.

On top of that, Cody Gakpo looks increasingly likely to be making the switch to Tottenham Hotspur.

The need for attackers is staring the Anfield hierarchy in the face and hopefully this could be the start of some movement on that front.

A double raid on the European champions would be quite the signal of intent…

title: ESPN insider sees Ohio State as 'Big Ten Sleeper' this season
description: ESPN insider Myron Medcalf believes the Ohio State basketball team can be a Big Ten sleeper and Elite Eight team this year.
fullText:
A year after being on the hot seat, Ohio State head coach Jake Diebler enters the 2026-27 season with lofty goals and has the Buckeyes slotted in many pre-season top 25 polls.

Ohio State brings in eight new players -- both transfers and freshmen -- nearly all of whom are expected to make some sort of impact this season, and that is combined with returnees and potential All-Big Ten players John Mobley Jr and Amare Bynum.

According to one ESPN insider, Ohio State could be the 'Big Ten Sleeper' this season.

"The Buckeyes could be a Big Ten sleeper, provided they pull the pieces together," Myron Medcalf wrote. "Doing so will demand another outstanding season from John Mobley Jr. (15.7 PPG, 41% from 3), who will play next to incoming five-star and projected top-10 draft pick Anthony Thompson. Jake Diebler also added a strong portal class, including Justin Pippen -- the son of NBA legend Scottie Pippen -- who led Cal in scoring last season. The Buckeyes went dancing this past March thanks to a late push. It's easy to predict Selection Sunday should feel more comfortable next year."

Thompson, who pledged to his in state Buckeyes over Indiana, is one of the more purely gifted athletes and freshmen that has played in the Ohio State program in quite some time. His skill alone, assuming his potential is reached this year, is enough to keep the Buckeyes in a good spot most of the year. Add in transfers like Pippen, Jimmie Williams, Curtis Givens, Andrija Jelavic and Josh Ojianwuna, and the core is set alongside Mobley and Bynum.

Ohio State is coming off of a 21-13 season last year and an eight-seed in the NCAA Tournament. The expectations are more this year.

Medcalf sees the Buckeyes as a potential Elite Eight sleeper as the team's ceiling, with 28 wins. On the flip side, a first round exit is the floor.

The Buckeyes are coming off of a trip to Puerto Rico which provided a good experience for such a new team, and will play Cincinnati and Butler in exhibitions before getting the season underway.

title: Notts and Durham reach One-Day Cup semi-finals
description: Jack Haynes and Kyle Verreyne hit centuries as Notts beat Yorkshire in the One-Day Cup quarter-finals, as Durham also win through.
fullText:
Nottinghamshire pulled off a glorious comeback day as they and Durham both won away from home to book their places in Sunday's One-Day Cup semi-finals.

Notts looked out for the count when they slumped to 1-3 chasing Yorkshire's 273-9 at Clifton Park, York - including two wickets in two balls for Ben Coad.

But, from 55-4, a 154-run stand between centurions Jack Haynes (116*) and Kyle Verreynne (105) transformed the contest and they went on to win by three wickets with eight balls to spare.

Notts, who have never reached the final of this competition since it moved from Lord's to their Trent Bridge home in 2021, now face an East Midlands derby in Sunday's semi against Group A winners and 2024 winners Leicestershire.

Durham's David Bedingham-inspired 162-run humbling of Lancashire at Old Trafford earned the visitors their seventh successful passage to a List A semi-final.

They will now play Group B winners Middlesex, who qualified automatically for a home semi with ease, winning seven of their eight group games.

The match will be played at Radlett, as Lord's is unavailable.

Durham were far too good for Lancashire as they recovered from a slightly sticky start to post a powerful 349-8 from their 50 overs.

Approaching halfway, Durham - including former England skipper Ben Stokes - were only on 110-3, but Bedingham (104) and Ollie Robinson (76) then shared a crucial stand of 149 in 16 overs.

Even when they were parted in the 41st over on 259-4, Durham still plundered a further 90 runs.

Stokes hit his second ball for six before being caught by Australian Marcus Harris at long off for 11, but Bedingham went on to complete his fifth hundred in all formats against Lancashire off just 87 balls before some late hitting from Colin Ackermann and captain Kasey Aldridge.

In reply, former Durham man Keaton Jennings and Josh Bohannon briefly looked in control - but both departed before Harris lucklessly removed a bail by treading on his stumps.

It was not Rocky Flintoff's day either as he departed for 22, one of four wickets for leg-spinner Shaq Ghafari as the hosts were bowled out for 187 to suffer the fifth heaviest defeat in their illustrious 63-year one-day cricket history.

Teenager Joe Moores - the nephew of Notts and former England head coach Peter Moores - was their mainstay, hitting four sixes in his 51 off 42 balls.

"Credit to Ollie Robinson," Bedingham told BBC Radio Newcastle. "He changed the game when he came in.

"I always thought 350 would be a tough chase. It put pressure on Lancashire. The bowlers were excellent and it was a fine all-round team effort."

"We were out-performed by Durham in all departments," Lancs head coach Steven Croft told BBC Radio Lancashire. "The toss was pretty important but we probably took a couple of backward steps.

"They batted well but, at halfway they probably had 30-40 runs over par and they carried that momentum forward. We didn't throw too many punches in that run chase. Rocky and Moorsey sort of showed the way."

An excellent first-team best score of 91 from youngster Will Bennison was the cornerstone of Yorkshire's 273-9, but it maybe should have been more as they lost momentum in mid-innings.

And, ultimately, it did not prove quite enough as in-form South African Verreynne came in to help Notts from their stuttering start with 105 off 123 balls.

After he was out, Haynes carried on the fine work as the former Worcestershire man got his side over the line with only his third List A century.

His former Pears team-mate Dillon Pennington, who had earlier struck four times with the ball, assisted at the end with two fours and a six in his 18-ball cameo of 22.

Earlier, after starting with the wickets of Freddie McCann and visiting skipper Haseeb Hameed, Coad claimed a fine 5-52 - but how different it might have been if Verreynne had not survived the hat-trick ball.

Notts, who last won a List A trophy at Lord's in 2017, now have a chance to follow Worcestershire as the latest winners of the trophy.

Haynes, who was playing his first game since July because of injury, said: "No matter how long it's been, you always think, 'have I forgotten how to bat or not?' So, it was nice to hit a couple out of the middle.

"Kyle out there with his class made it a lot easier for me. Over the course of the competition, Kyle's been brilliant."

Yorkshire head coach Anthony McGrath admitted his side should have posted a 300 plus total in their innings.

"That would probably have been enough. We probably just pushed the button a little bit too early and then lost wickets," he said.

"You've got to give them credit. Hundreds win games with a bat, Verreynne and Haynes both got hundreds and batted brilliantly there. But I can't fault our lads, we fought all the way through."

title: Bryce Harper makes request to MLB after Phillies win against Twins
description: Philadelphia Phillies outfielder Bryce Harper offered an idea about the Field of Dreams game.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies and Minnesota Twins faced off Thursday in the 2026 Field of Dreams game in Dyersville, Iowa. The Phillies took the win 7-1, hammering three home runs during the contest.

It was star slugger Kyle Schwarber doing the biggest damage, going 2-for-5 with two home runs and three RBIs. Outfielder Bryce Harper got involved as well, going 1-for-4 with a walk and a fourth inning RBI single.

It was the third Field of Dreams game overall and first since 2022 due to construction in the area. Harper said before the game that he would like the game to be an entire series instead, as reported by Tim Kelly of On Pattinson.

For a whole three-game series to happen at Field of Dreams, there would need to be more permanent housing available in the area. Dyersville is a town of just over 4,300 people and about 70 miles from any interstate highway.

To build more hotels and other lodging would be excellent as far as a potential game/series goes. However, that could end up compromising the charm of the town and game atmosphere.

For now, it is just the one-off game before the teams return to one of their parks to host the rest of the series. The Phillies and Twins will play two more at Target Field in Minneapolis on Saturday night and Sunday afternoon.

MLB wasted no time in scheduling the next Field of Dreams matchup. The Kansas City Royals and Boston Red Sox will square off in Iowa on August 12, 2027.

The star outfielder has appeared in all 123 Phillies games this year, slashing .253/.373/.495 (.868 OPS) with 25 home runs and 72 RBIs. The 33-year-old has remained consistent during his 13-year, $330 million contract.

After Philadelphia's 9-19 start this season, they have managed to climb back in the race. They are currently 65-58, second place in the National League East. They trail the Atlanta Braves by nine games.

The Phillies occupy the third and final NL Wild Card spot for the time being. They will need Harper and Schwarber to get hot as the postseason draws closer in order to make it in.

title: Giants call up Jonah Cox and Turner Hill
description: Grant McCray and Nate Furman have been optioned.
fullText:
The San Francisco Giants made a series of moves on Friday, ahead of their series opener against the Colorado Rockies, as they're bringing up a pair of youngsters to replace a pair of youngsters.

As was reported on Thursday, the Giants are calling up outfielder Turner Hill to make his MLB debut. Hill is a tremendous story, as the 27-year old went undrafted in 2023 but has steadily rose through the ranks with strong defense, good base stealing, and sensational contact skills. He was on a 26-game hitting streak in AAA Sacramento, and in 88 games at the level this year posted a .950 OPS and a 148 wRC+, with just an 8.5% strikeout rate. The Giants are surely excited to get a long look at him over the next six weeks as they try to figure out which of their young players can contribute in 2027.

Joining Hill is Jonah Cox, who makes his return to the Majors following a brief stint in AAA. Cox was shockingly called up straight from AA in June, but played sparingly and looked fairly overmatched (while he collected a home run and a double off of position players, he hit just 5-24 with 15 strikeouts against MLB pitchers). The hair-on-fire 25-year old, who is arguably the best defensive outfielder in the system and the best base stealer, was injured in July, and got his first taste of AAA during a rehab assignment. After finishing that rehab assignment he was optioned back to AAA. In 11 games with Sacramento, Cox hit a stunning 22-47 with six extra-base hits and five walks, albeit some underlying metrics that should still give the Giants a little pause about his readiness for success at the next level.

With Jung Hoo Lee playing almost every game in right field, it seems likely that left and center will be handled by Hill and Drew Gilbert when a right-hander is on the mound, and by Cox and Victor Bericoto when facing a lefty.

Hill and Cox replace outfielder Grant McCray and second baseman Nate Furman, who were both optioned back to Sacramento. It's especially tough news for McCray, who has to feel that his time with the organization might be nearing an end (though he has another option year after this one). While McCray had a huge home run in late July, he's looked wholly uncomfortable in the batter's box since getting called back to the Majors. He hasn't collected a single hit in August, and since the last game of July he's gone 0-20 with five walks and eight strikeouts. He's hitting just .081/.227/.162 on the year, for a 22 wRC+, and has also hit below average when in AAA this season.

As for Furman, he barely got on the field, and will have to wait to collect his first Major League hit. He was called up right before the trade deadline, presumably to give the team an option if Luis Arráez were traded mid-game. But given that he's limited to just second base, and that the Giants are clearly invested in seeing if Osleivis Basabe or Christian Koss can emerge as a viable backup infielder option, there just wasn't playing time for the lefty, whose proper developmental place was always in AAA. Furman got into just five games in his two weeks with the Giants, and hit 0-6 with two walks and a strikeout.

title: Britain's Finlay Tarling dies in Volta a Portugal accident
description: British cyclist Finlay Tarling dies at the age of 19 in a serious accident during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.
fullText:
British cyclist Finlay Tarling has died aged 19 after an accident during the eighth stage of the Volta a Portugal.

Tarling, the younger brother of Netcompany-Ineos rider Josh, had raced for Great Britain on the road and track.

The Welshman was competing for the NSN Development Team when the incident occurred on the 166.8km route from Melgaco to Fafe.

In a statement, NSN said: "We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal today.

"Fin was a much loved member of our team but most importantly, he was a son, a brother, and a friend to so many. He will be deeply missed.

"Our deepest condolences go out to Fin's parents Michael and Dawn, his brother Josh, and everyone who was lucky enough to call Fin a friend."

In a post on X, the race organisers and the Portuguese Cycling Federation expressed their "most heartfelt condolences to the family of Finlay Tarling, to his team-mates, to the NSN Development Team, and to all his friends and loved ones".

It added that the racing was stopped and the scheduled podium ceremony would not take place as a sign of "respect and mourning".

Portuguese president Antonio Jose Seguro added that Tarling's death had "plunged the peloton, the tournament and the host nation into mourning".

British Cycling's performance director Stephen Park, added: "All of us at British Cycling are heartbroken to learn of the tragic passing of Finlay Tarling at the Volta a Portugal.

"Fin was a talented rider with a fantastic future ahead of him, a loyal teammate and an all-round brilliant young man.

"Our deepest sympathies are with his parents and brother, Josh at this tragic time."

The Volta a Portugal got under way in Lisbon on 5 August and is raced over 10 stages, concluding in Porto on 16 August.

Tarling looked to be following in the footsteps of his older brother Josh as a time trial specialist.

He finished in third in the under-23 men's individual time trial at the British Championships in June and competed in the Tour of Britain just under 12 months ago.

title: Nigeria misses Women's World Cup for first time ever after playoff loss
description: After falling in the WAFCON quarterfinals, the Super Falcons couldn't beat South Africa and will be absent from the 2027 tournament in Brazil.
fullText:
The 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil will be missing something that has been at every previous edition: Nigeria.

The Super Falcons fell 2-1 to South Africa in a playoff that sent the winner to FIFA's intercontinental playoff.

Nigeria has appeared at all nine editions of the Women's World Cup since the tournament launched in its current format in 1991. Prior to this edition of the Women's African Cup of Nations, which also served as World Cup qualification, Nigeria had never missed the semifinal.

Nigeria knew its hopes were in danger after a stunning quarterfinal loss to Cameroon, in which Nigeria put nine shots on goal but saw them all denied by Cameroon goalkeeper Michaely Bihina. Maéva Nyadjou's goal in the 19th minute proved to be the difference in a 1-0 Cameroon win.

That sent Nigeria into the must-win match with South Africa, but a goal from Tigres attacker Thembi Kgatlana in the 56th minute and another from captain Refiloe Jane in the 77th meant Nigeria would need a furious rally to have any hope of still making it to Brazil.

That nearly came off, with Christy Ucheibe scoring a stoppage-time penalty and Chicago Stars defender Michelle Alozie putting a shot on target with one of the final touches of the game. South Africa goalkeeper Kaylin Swart stuck out her leg to deny Alozie's effort, one of five saves on the day, and Nigeria were eliminated from World Cup contention.

Malawi, Cameroon, Algeria and Morocco are the qualified teams from the African region with South Africa joined by Ghana in the play-in.

After beating Nigeria, Cameroon got past host Morocco in a penalty shootout, earning a place in the final against Malawi, which beat Algeria thanks to a double from Tabitha Chaŵinga and a goal from her sister, KC Current forward Temwa Chaŵinga.

FIFA announced this week it will reveal the schedule of matches for the 2027 tournament on August 20 as it also conducts the draw for the intercontinental playoff. The draw for the tournament itself is expected to take place in December with the tournament kicking off June 24, 2027.

title: White Sox make savvy waiver claim of ex-Tigers, Red Sox catcher
description: This is a very savvy move for the White Sox this August after the trade deadline.
fullText:
White Sox make savvy waiver claim of ex-Tigers, Red Sox catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Chicago White Sox went into the MLB trade deadline with a need behind the plate at catcher. They explored some options, but only wound up with Joey Bart.

Unfortunately, Bart got hurt, landed on the injured list, and is now going to miss a lot of time. So, with a need at catcher once again, the White Sox got a perfect opportunity to upgrade their depth chart.

According to Chris Cotillo of MassLive.com, the White Sox have claimed former Detroit Tigers veteran catcher Jake Rogers off waivers from the Boston Red Sox. It's a savvy move and is a very nice addition to the catcher room this summer at no cost.

"Sources: Jake Rogers to White Sox via waiver claim," Cotillo reports Thursday afternoon.

Rogers joins Drew Romo and Edgar Quero in the catcher room, as Kyle Teel and Bart are both on the injured list. Romo has a .508 OPS this season, while Quero has a .541 OPS.

The catcher position is one the White Sox clearly needed to upgrade. Fortunately, they've found their upgrade in Rogers, the longtime Tigers catcher.

The 31-year-old veteran was recently acquired in the Adley Rutschman trade between the Red Sox and Baltimore Orioles, which came after he was DFA'd by the Tigers earlier this season.

He was then DFA'd by Boston a few days ago when Rutschman was activated off the injured list. That gave the White Sox a prime opportunity to land a decent catcher option.

MORE: MLB experts voted Red Sox's Adley Rutschman trade as most surprising by wide margin

This season, in 40 games, Rogers has 104 at-bats with a .183 batting average, but a .617 OPS. That's not anything to be overly excited about, but it's a clear step better than Quero and Romo's offensive production this season.

With the Red Sox, however, Rogers had a 1.389 OPS in nine plate appearances, getting three hits in six at-bats with four runs scored, two doubles, two RBIs, and two walks with one sacrifice fly.

He obviously won't be posting such a high OPS for the White Sox, but it's clear that Rogers is a legitimately decent starting catcher option for the White Sox and is a very savvy mid-August pickup off waivers for Chicago as they try to win the AL Central.

title: Kim Mulkey, LSU add Russian post Anna Minaeva to 2026-27 roster
description: LSU women's basketball officially announced to addition of 17-year-old Russian forward Anna Minaeva to the 2026-27 roster.
fullText:
BATON ROUGE — The final piece of the puzzle is finally in place for 2026-27 for Kim Mulkey and the LSU women's basketball team.

LSU announced the official addition of 6-foot-5 forward Anna Minaeva from Russia on Aug. 14. After months of speculation of when Mulkey would bring in Minaeva, who had rumored to be who the LSU staff had zeroed in on, the waiting game is over for both parties.

Minaeva landed in the United States on Thursday. She is the second international signee this offseason for LSU joining Spaniard Noa Morro, who's been with LSU for much of this summer.

LSU VS UCONN IN NASHVILLE Kim Mulkey v Geno Auriemma. LSU women's hoops to face UConn in Nashville

The 17-year-old Russian has been playing professional basketball in her home country mostly for MBA Moscow-2, the second level squad before being promoted to the top flight team where she averaged 5.6 points with four rebounds in just 12 games.

At 6-5, Minaeva, albeit young, brings much-needed size to the low block for Mulkey and the Tigers. Both Ukrainian Kate Koval and sophomore Grace Knox have loads of experience with LSU and there won't be a lot of pressure for Minaeva to adapt and develop quickly.

Minaeva is known for her ability to play defense without getting into foul trouble and can time up her jumps to block shots, aspects of post play that LSU struggled with at times last season. The footwork she possesses in screen-and-pops and pick-and-rolls will bolster Mulkey's offensive system.

title: BC Football Countdown to Kickoff 2026: Duke Preview
description: Boston College will face a new-look Blue Devils team this season.
fullText:
Halloween falls on a Saturday this year and that means Boston College will be in action.

The Eagles will face off with ACC foe Duke in what is its second straight road game and part of a stretch of three out of four.

Head Coaches: Bill O'Brien, Boston College; Manny Diaz, Duke

When: Saturday, October 31 at TBD

Where: Wallace Wade Stadium in Durham, North Carolina

The history between these two teams dates back to 1927 when they first played in Chestnut Hill, Mass. After meetings in three consecutive seasons, they did not play until 2006. There has been a total of nine matchups between Boston College and Duke with the Eagles holding a 5-4 advantage. Duke has won three of the last four.

What a year it was for the Blue Devils. Duke began 1-2 after a loss to Tulane before ripping off three straight wins. The Blue Devils had another bad loss to UConn midseason but won the final three games, including the ACC Championship against Virginia. The Blue Devils would go on to win the Sun Bowl, 42-39, over Arizona State.

Darian Mensah was going to return to Duke this fall but the transfer portal era got in the way. Miami came calling with what has to be a nice offer to play quarterback and he headed to South Beach.

This leaves the Blue Devils without their leader who threw for close to 4,000 yards and 34 touchdowns last year. In comes Walker Eget from San Jose State. He has been thrown to turning the ball over but has a big-time arm. Dan Mahan has not played yet but was a highly-valued recruit last year as well.

Not only did Mensah head south, but Duke lost its top pass catcher as Cooper Barkate will join his quarterback in Miami. He led Duke with 1,106 yards and seven touchdowns last season. Qua'Sean Brown (Virginia Tech) and Sahmir Hagans (graduated) are also gone. This leaves Duke without its top three pass catchers.

This means tight end Jeremiah Halsey will have to take on more responsibility while transfers Jared Richardson and Javen Nicholas will be thrown into the mix right away.

It also looks like Nate Sheppard will be relied upon more heavily after an All-ACC season where he totaled 1,132 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns. He will be running behind a new offensive like with Braden Miller (Cal) and Nick Del Grande (Coastal Carolina) coming to play tackle, joining center Matt Craycraft and guard Jordan Larsen.

Manny Diaz knows how to coach up a defense and we saw this last season.

This defense last year was strong up front and took the ball away often but struggled on third down and in the passing game.

The Blue Devils forced 24 turnovers last season and multiple in seven games. The middle of the defense will be just as good with Luke Mergott and Kendall Johnson returning. The duo combined for 127 tackles last season. Throw a healthy Nick Morris in the mix and the linebackers are elite.

The defense needed four new starters up front after coming away with 11 or more tackles for loss in six games.

The secondary lost Chandler Rivers and Caleb Weaver as well. The defense allowed 276.8 passing yards per game and 45% or worse on third downs eight times.

This being a late October matchup means we will likely know the direction of Boston College's season by this point. The major question is — can the Eagles pull off an upset over the reigning ACC champs?

Duke's offense will look completely different but by this point of the season, it will not be a new-look group anymore. It will be interesting to see if the Eagles can take advantage of the new faces though and get in the backfield. This is another game where the Eagles will be getting points and at this time, it is hard to imagine an upset. But anything is possible!

Will the Eagles be able to earn a statement victory heading into November?

title: Stolen Super Bowl ring has Bernie Kosar asking Jerry Jones for a replacement
description: Bernie Kosar asked Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones for a replacement after his original Super Bowl ring was stolen.
fullText:
Stolen Super Bowl ring has Bernie Kosar asking Jerry Jones for a replacement originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Bernie Kosar is still remembered well by fans of the Cleveland Browns. He guided the franchise to three AFC Championship games during the late 1980s, and is considered one of their best quarterbacks ever.

He later went to the Dallas Cowboys, where he played as a backup quarterback. He managed to win Super Bowl XXVIII in the 1993 season, the only time he won it in his career. Kosar is now asking his former franchise's owner for help after a horrible incident.

Kosar was drafted by the Browns in 1985 and spent eight seasons with them as the starting quarterback. After being released in 1993, he joined the Cowboys as the backup to Troy Aikman for one season. Though he only played for four games, that was the only season he managed to win the Lombardi Trophy, a career high for him.

He did play an important role in the NFC Championship game against the San Francisco 49ers, after Aikman was unavailable in the second half of the game due to a concussion. He was also heavily involved during Super Bowl week, helping to prepare the team with offensive coordinator Norv Turner and even appeared in the final play of the Super Bowl game against the Buffalo Bills.

Kosar recently appeared on the August 12, 2026, episode of The Sage Steele Show. He revealed that the Super Bowl XXVIII championship ring he earned with the Cowboys was stolen. He asked for Cowboys owner Jerry Jones to get a replacement ring for the one he lost.

He said, "I lost it, so I can't wear it. And Jerry, I'm going to be calling you because it got stolen. I'm going to be calling you for another one, bro. So, please help me out again."

So far, Jones has not yet responded to this plea for help. Details about the theft are still unknown, and it remains to be seen if the Cowboys owner can manage another Super Bowl ring for him. Kosar recently got compared to one current player of the Browns.

Browns legend Hanford Dixon recently compared franchise quarterback Shedeur Sanders with Kosar. Kosar and Dixon were teammates, and the comparison was praiseworthy for Sanders. Speaking on the BIGPLAY Cleveland Show, he said, "I see Bernie Kosar. And what I mean by that is, one thing we knew about Bernie, is that Bernie was very confident. I mean, he was a guy that believed in his ability, he knew that he could play, and knew that he could play quarterback."

He added, "Shedeur is the same way. He's a very confident guy. Some people call him cocky. I don't have a problem with him being cocky. But I think this guy is very, very confident. He knows that he can play, he believes that he can play. He's the type of guy at the quarterback position that a team rallies themselves around him. They'll get behind this guy if we give him the chance to prove himself."

Bernie Kosar will be hoping that Sanders manages to emulate him, and that the Cowboys get him a replacement ring.

title: Sunderland Are In The Running To Sign This Ligue 1 Wide Player: Should Le Bris Get Him On Board?
description: In a recent report, Foot Mercato mentioned that Sunderland are in the running to sign Olympique Marseille wide player Timothy Weah. It has been claimed that the Black Cats have shown interest in recru...
fullText:
In a recent report, Foot Mercato mentioned that Sunderland are in the running to sign Olympique Marseille wide player Timothy Weah. It has been claimed that the Black Cats have shown interest in recruiting the United States talent, who remains focused on his Marseille career.

Weah managed to shine at times with his performances for the French club in Ligue 1 last season when he put in a handful of solid performances for them on the right flank. The 26-year-old registered a couple of goals and secured two assists in 29 league matches for Marseille in the previous campaign.

The United States sensation is currently among the most talented wide players in Ligue 1. Hence, the Black Cats would do well to get a deal done for him this off-season.

His current contract at the French club will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for Sunderland to land him on a cut-price deal later this year.

SANTA ANA, CALIFORNIA – JUNE 06: Timothy Weah of the United States arrives for the FIFA World Cup 2026 at John Wayne Airport on June 06, 2026 in Santa Ana, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images)

Weah doesn't mind putting in a hard-working performance for his team defensively when needed. He is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet and can engineer the odd chance for his teammates to find the back of the net.

The United States talent can shoot the ball with power from long range and did well to add a few goals and assists to his game last season. Weah is primarily a right-sided wide player but can also fill in as a right-back if told to do so. However, only time will tell whether he can adapt to the physical style and high intensity of the Premier League if the Black Cats manage to sign him later this year.

We can expect Weah to enhance the quality of Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris' squad. He is good enough to fight for a regular first-team place at the Stadium of Light next season.

At 26, Weah has his best years ahead of him, which makes him a decent option for the Wearside club to consider this summer. He will also help Sunderland compete across all fronts in the coming years. Thus, Le Bris should focus on getting him on board this month.

title: Moro Ojomo, Fred Johnson fought at Eagles' practice on Thursday
description: The preseason has advanced to the point at which most fights happen during joint practices.
fullText:
The preseason has advanced to the point at which most fights happen during joint practices. But there are still squabbles among players on the same squad.

Via Tim McManus of ESPN, Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo and tackle Fred Johnson got into a fight on Thursday, which eventually required them to be pulled apart. Twice.

As McManus explains it, things got started when Johnson gave Ojomo a late shove during team drills. Ojomo braced to fight Johnson.

The players weren't removed from action.

On the next play, Johnson blocked Ojomo to the ground. Johnson landed on Ojomo with his full body weight. The players traded punches before they were separated.

Not long after that, Ojomo worked his way through a cluster of bodies and dove at Johnson's knees.

The players were separated again. Coach Nick Sirianni, G.M. Howie Roseman, and the multi-titled Big Dom worked to calm Johnson down.

So, yes, it's time for the Eagles to direct their aggression to others. They'll open the preseason on Saturday night against the Ravens.

title: Here are the best Jayden Daniels LSU number memes taking over the internet
description: A look at social media's jokes about Daniels' debacle regarding his LSU No. 5 jersey.
fullText:
Here are the best Jayden Daniels LSU number memes taking over the internet originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Despite being an incredibly gifted young quarterback in the NFL, Jayden Daniels has put himself through a lot of flak in an attempt to preserve the prestige that is his LSU No. 5 jersey.

Earlier this month, the Washington Commanders quarterback sent a cease-and-desist to his alma mater after the school allowed cornerback DJ Pickett to rep Daniels' college number.

Since the struggle emerged, social media has had a field day in dragging Daniels through the mud. The consensus, regardless of whether or not someone has a Tigers or Commanders fandom, is that the endless collection of No. 5 memes is a laugh factory.

Here is a look at social media's jokes about Daniels' debacle regarding his LSU No. 5 jersey.

MORE: Why did Jayden Daniels send LSU a cease and desist?

Since Daniels' cease and desist became a mainstream news story, social media has been stirred up into a frenzy, compiling different ways to remove the No. 5 from popular everyday things. From ticket companies pretending to remove buying five tickets as an option to jokes about Alan Jackson changing his song title to "It's Four o'clock Somewhere," the creations have been near endless.

Here's a round-up of the most hilarious memes from the No. 5 situation:

NFL parody account Richard Johnson shared a few jokes regarding Daniels' number:

On Thursday, news broke of LSU giving sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett the No. 5 to wear on the gridiron this upcoming season. Technically, Daniels' number worn for the Tigers, and his current number for the Commanders, was never retired.

Daniels sent a cease-and-desist letter to LSU on Aug. 5, requesting that LSU no longer use his name, image and likeness (NIL) after letting another player wear his previous collegiate number.

"The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU's decision to give Jayden's number to another player," Daniels' spokesperson said, per ESPN. "Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university."

The statement continued, saying LSU's decision "feels like a failure to honor the significance of what Jayden accomplished at LSU," and claiming that "Jayden made it clear he did not want his number given to another player."

On Thursday, Daniels posted a statement stating that "there are issues to be worked out between my team and LSU" and ensuring those interested that his "sole personal focus" is on the Commanders.

Jayden Daniels just posted this on Instagram relating to the situation with LSU: pic.twitter.com/0iUJXcek6Z

Former LSU coach Brian Kelly, who recruited Pickett, told ESPN that the No. 5 was promised to the cornerback, but said he held off on giving him the number because of Daniels' objection.

"I just wasn't prepared to do it until we got a full commitment from another Heisman Trophy winner," Kelly said. "We didn't want to issue No. 9, so you can't treat one differently from the other."

Current Cincinnati Bengals and former Tigers quarterback Joe Burrow donned the No. 9 under his nameplate during his LSU days. Despite winning a national championship in 2019, his number also is not technically retired, but a player has not matched Burrow's number since he departed for the NFL.

title: San Francisco to host 2028 MLB All-Star Game
description: San Francisco will host the 2028 Major League All-Star Game, the Midsummer Classic returning to the Giants' Oracle Park 21 years after it hosted in 2007."With its passionate fanbase, world-class ballpark, and rich baseball history, San Francisco will be an outstanding host for All-Star Week, which culminates in one of Major League Baseball's best traditions, the Midsummer Classic," MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said in a statement on Friday.
fullText:
San Francisco will host the 2028 Major League All-Star Game, the Midsummer Classic returning to the Giants' Oracle Park 21 years after it hosted in 2007.

"With its passionate fanbase, world-class ballpark, and rich baseball history, San Francisco will be an outstanding host for All-Star Week, which culminates in one of Major League Baseball's best traditions, the Midsummer Classic," MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said in a statement on Friday.

"We look forward to bringing the excitement of All-Star Week and the celebration of baseball to the Bay Area."

The last time the All-Star Game was held at the waterfront ballpark, Japanese star Ichiro Suzuki was named Most Valuable Player after hitting the first inside-the-park home run in the history of the mid-season exhibition.

The event will mark another major sporting celebration for the Bay Area. The San Francisco 49ers' Levi's Stadium hosted the Super Bowl in February and six World Cup matches last month, and the Golden State Warriors hosted the NBA All-Star Game in February of 2025.

Wrigley Field, venerable home of the Chicago Cubs, is scheduled to host next season's All-Star game.

title: Miami junior RB Jordan Lyle arrested on charges of reckless driving and fleeing law enforcement
description: Lyle faces felony complaints of aggravated fleeing and eluding law enforcement and a misdemeanor complaint of reckless driving. He was released on $55,000 bond.
fullText:
Miami junior running back Jordan Lyle was arrested on Thursday on charges of aggravated fleeing and eluding law enforcement, according to court records in Broward County, Florida.

The aggravated fleeing and eluding law enforcement are each felony complaints. Lyle also faces a misdemeanor complaint of reckless driving.

"We are aware of an incident involving student-athlete Jordan Lyle," a University of Miami spokesperson said in a statement on Friday, via the Miami Herald. "As due legal process runs its course, we will have no further comment at this time."

Lyle, 20, was booked into the Broward Main Jail of the Sheriff's Office on an arrest warrant from the Sunrise Police Department and was released later in the day. The charges against Lyle carry a combined $55,000 bond.

Last season as a sophomore, Lyle rushed for 108 yards and 1 touchdown on 35 carries. He was limited to six games due to a high ankle sprain suffered in the Hurricanes' season-opening 27-24 win over Notre Dame. As a freshman, Lyle compiled 400 rushing yards on 54 carries with 4 TDs.

The 6-foot, 205-pound running back was in a battle with fellow junior Char'Mar Brown, sophomore Girard Pringle Jr. and freshman Javian Mallory for the No. 2 spot on Miami's depth chart behind starter Mark Fletcher Jr., who rushed for 1,192 yards and 12 TDs last season.

Earlier this week, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said Lyle appeared to be back to "full speed" in practices.

"I see the Jordan Lyle that we saw a year ago in many respects, but with better physical traits," Cristobal told reporters, via Canes InSight.

"Jordan has taken strength and conditioning very seriously," he added. "I think he's certainly improved his [change of direction], his excel, decel rate. He's healthy, which I think is a really important part. I don't think people really knew the extent of how banged up he was last year."

Lyle is a native of Fort Lauderdale, Florida, and came to Miami out of St. Thomas Aquinas High School. He was ranked as the No. 6 running back nationally by Rivals and the No. 114 player overall. Originally, Lyle committed to Ohio State before flipping to Miami.

Miami comes into the 2026-27 season ranked No. 7 after going 13-3 last season and playing for the College Football Playoff national championship.

title: Generous 12-year-old has wish fulfilled by Eagles after helping homeless

fullText:
A 12-year-old boy from Philadelphia who has dedicated his own Make-A-Wish experience to helping others saw one of his personal dreams fulfilled Thursday.

Sam Okyere, who has been battling a blood disorder, used his wish to host a "family day" at Families Forward, a West Philadelphia homeless shelter, choosing to give back rather than receive something for himself.

But Sam's next wish was to meet Hurts. The Eagles got word and it came true.

Hurts and Saquon Barkley stopped by after camp Thursday to spend time with Sam.

"I heard you were trying to do a good deed and you wanted to help and serve others. To see you doing it at such a young age is mighty impressive. Keep it up," Hurts said.

Sam and Hurts bonded over video games, including NBA2K and Mario Super Smash Bros., while Sam encouraged Barkley to get back into LEGO building.

title: Former FSU QB Jordan Travis shines in new role at Pensacola booster event
description: Former FSU quarterback Jordan Travis discussed his new role connecting with Seminole fans at a local booster event in Pensacola.
fullText:
The remembrance of good times rolled through Seville Quarter's Heritage Hall as Jordan Travis captivated a sold out gathering of Florida State Seminoles' supporters.

So much has changed, of course.

Both with FSU football fortunes and in Travis' life since the former star quarterback sustained a career-devastating leg injury on November 18, 2023, as the Seminoles barreled toward an undefeated regular season.

"Obviously, I thought the NFL was my dream and my future and things changed really quickly," said Travis, prior to joining the stage on Thursday Aug. 13 at the annual Greater Pensacola Seminole Club Kickoff Party, alongside Jeff Culhane, now in his fifth year as voice of the Seminoles, and Gene Deckerhoff the retired broadcasting legend, who held that role for 43 years.

Together, they shared stories, told jokes, answered questions and brought hope in a unique setting that was different than so many preseason booster gatherings.

In July, Travis officially joined Seminoles Boosters in a lead role to help launch Seminoles United, a separate component of the organization designed to expand connection to FSU supporters in a variety of ways.

One of those ways is speaking to FSU booster clubs throughout the state. It was Travis' first time in Pensacola.

"I had no idea what I was going to end up doing," said Travis, 26, a West Palm Beach native, whose final season at FSU produced record-setting results.  "But this opportunity came up, they (FSU Boosters) created this position and it's been a dream."

Before a standing-room-only gathering, Travis helped answer questions from the crowd about a variety of topics.

It was a feel-good night for local FSU supporters, who reacted with standing ovations when each of the three men were announced to the stage.

The program ended on this night with Travis planning a spear into a bullseye on stage.

Travis related that it has rekindled the rush of nervous adrenaline he felt before games. He was reminded of what FSU coach Mike Norvell often told the team that it's essential "to be comfortable with being uncomfortable."

"If there is not anything uncomfortable, then there is not a lot of growth," said Travis, who grew into becoming one of the best quarterbacks in FSU history. He holds the team's all-time records for touchdowns, total offense, and is the only quarterback in the program's decorated history with more than 50 passing touchdowns and 12 rushing touchdowns

"So, going up on stage is uncomfortable for me," he said. "It's not something I do naturally. But it's like in football when there were days I was down and I threw interceptions and it didn't feel good.

"Having myself in that situation again, just getting up on stage going through it, and it feels so good. It feels like I am in a game again, so that is good."

Travis signed autographs for more than an hour before the program began. He met everyone with a smile and connected with greetings.

Travis was chosen by the New York Jets in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, while he was still trying to recover from the serious leg injury suffered in the second half of the second-to-last game of the 2023 regular season.

He never played for the Jets. In April 2025, he announced his retirement from football and it led to the opportunity that he now has with the FSU athletic program.

"He has become such a key part of our Seminole Booster family," said Culhane, who made his third visit to Pensacola to address a preseason event. "Seminoles United is a new platform.

"It's new app that is content creation for our fans and designed to unite all Seminoles. And tell success stories that are going on with FSU athletics.

"Jordan is the perfect person to be that face and that voice right now," Culhane said. "What an unbelievable football player, but when you listen to him speak (at these events), you begin to understand the person that he is.

"He is just such a genuine, kind and caring individual. And you see why the teams he was on rallied behind him and brought us some of the greatest memories of Mike Norvell era."

Travis said his role in meeting so many new faces provides an opportunity to directly impact FSU fans.

"My job is really cool," Travis said. "It is about community. It is about being loved. We all have the same goal to love on Florida State. My job is to make people who are Seminoles fans across the nation all feel like they are part of it."

The FSU gathering Aug. 13 was part of several connections in Pensacola. The famed "Graffiti Bridge" was painted to welcome FSU supporters prior to the event.

The FSU vs. Auburn "Fall Ball" baseball scrimmage sold out of seats in less than 36 hours after going on sale Aug. 11. The game is set for October 10 at Blue Wahoos Stadium.

That same day, the FSU men's basketball team will face Mississippi State in a preseason game at the Pensacola Bay Center. And on Nov. 29, the FSU women's basketball team will play UWF in the Argos first season as an NCAA Division I member.

"I love coming here. Pensacola Beach is beautiful, it's paradise," Culhane said. "I know there are different (college) brands that plant their flag here, but to me, Pensacola is a Seminole town."

Bill Vilona is a retired Pensacola News Journal sports columnist and now senior writer for Pensacola Blue Wahoos. He can be reached at bvilona@bluewahoos.com

title: Spurs predicted to outbid Lakers, Knicks for $63M NBA champion to pair with Victor Wembanmyama
description: The San Antonio Spurs can still add on to the roster. In this potential deal, they get a proven veteran that has won an NBA championship.
fullText:
Spurs predicted to outbid Lakers, Knicks for $63M NBA champion to pair with Victor Wembanmyama originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The San Antonio Spurs are coming off an NBA Finals appearance in which they lost in five games, despite holding leads down the stretch in several contests. San Antonio is a young team that appears poised to contend for years to come.

The Spurs have made it a priority to add veteran leadership this offseason. Their summer began with the signing of Tobias Harris to a two-year deal.

"Free agent forward Tobias Harris has agreed to a two-year, $31 million deal with the San Antonio Spurs, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday. Harris, 33, is leaving the Detroit Pistons after helping lead a franchise turnaround over the past two seasons. Now the productive veteran known for shotmaking and floor spacing in the frontcourt joins a young Western Conference contender after the Spurs and agent Torrel Harris of Unique Sports Management worked through a deal," ESPN wrote.

San Antonio could still add another veteran to its locker room to help mentor its young core. Bleacher Report's Dan Favale believes the Spurs could sign NBA champion Bruce Brown.

"None of Brown's other connective skills are a mirage. He keeps the ball moving; can reach the basket on or off the rock; knows how to cut and relocate in the half-court; keeps defenses guessing from short-roll territory; and is someone who can be moved up or down the positional spectrum if he's coming off the bench," Favale wrote.

Brown is one of the more dependable role players available in free agency and has drawn interest from several teams around the league.

"After helping the Denver Nuggets win an NBA championship, Bruce Brown is looking to cash in as a free agent this offseason. Per SNY's IanBegley, Brown is expected to meet with the Los Angeles, Lakers, New York Knicks, Houston Rockets, Dallas Mavericks and Indiana Pacers," Bleacher Report's Adam Wells wrote.

Brown has built his career as a true role player, embracing whatever responsibilities his team needs from him. For the Spurs, that versatility could make him an ideal addition to a young roster.

Brown has earned $63 million throughout his NBA career, but his value to San Antonio would extend beyond his on-court production. The Spurs are focused on building around Victor Wembanyama, and adding a veteran like Brown could give the young superstar another experienced teammate who can mentor him and help him navigate the demands of winning at the highest level.

title: Freshman safety displaying growth at Washington football fall camp
description: Freshman safety Gavin Day has displayed some significant growth through the early days of fall practice.
fullText:
Through the early days of fall camp, freshman safety Gavin Day has made the most of his opportunities with the Washington Huskies.

The 6-foot-3, 195-pound former four-star recruit has made his presence felt in the secondary thanks to his high-end range, athleticism, and physicality, building on a strong showing during spring practice.

Now, as position coach Taylor Mays looks to fill out his depth chart, Day has continued to make plays and shown off his value. On Thursday, the product of Faith Lutheran High School in Las Vegas, Nevada, stepped in front of a pass from quarterback Treston Kini McMillan, intended for wide receiver Justice Williams in the end zone, for his first interception of fall camp and returned the pass to midfield before he was pushed out of bounds.

"Gavin Day is improving," Mays said on Thursday. "I would say he's definitely improving from where he was in the spring to now; he's doing the things that we need him to do, that he wants to do for himself to become a player that can contribute this year. So, he's getting there. He still has a little bit of a ways to go, but he's definitely on pace for what we expect out of him going into his freshman year."

The Seattle native and three-time First Team All-American in his college career at USC, where he played a similar style to what Day showed on his high school film, was very detailed when asked what's next in the freshman's development.

"I think with a young guy, it's just how consistent can they be?" Mays continued. "Sometimes you have young guys that are just wild men on the field and still playing like it's high school football. But sometimes we have guys that are very tentative and thinking too much, playing too slow. And so I think Gavin, like most freshmen, is kind of just a mix of both of those."

"So we like them to, especially at safety, if you're in the middle of the field or in a deep zone, we can't have an error there, 'because a lot of times, that's a touchdown. So it's just the consistency part. The physical part I know will come with his body's development, but just the consistency would be the biggest thing that we're looking for from him. But he's on pace right now."

This article originally appeared on Huskies Wire: Freshman safety displaying growth at Washington football fall camp
