title: Can Chelsea go from 10th to title again?
description: With a new manager at the helm in Xabi Alonso, can Chelsea go from 10th to the Premier League title like they did a decade ago?
fullText:
Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League 10 years ago but incredibly were champions of England just a year later under new manager Antonio Conte.

After finishing in the same position last season, with no European football again and a new manager in Xabi Alonso, can the Blues repeat the feat?

Chelsea's Premier League record in 2025-26 is almost identical to when they finished mid-table under interim manager Guus Hiddink a decade ago.

With just one more goal scored and one more conceded, they finished with the same goal difference and just two points more than they did in 2015-16.

Few would have imagined back then that after finishing 31 points behind champions Leicester and below the likes of Southampton, West Ham and Stoke, Chelsea's players would be the ones lifting the Premier League trophy the following season.

After starting the campaign playing a back four, a 3-0 defeat at Arsenal in just their sixth game saw Conte switch his side to a back three. The impact was tremendous as they won their next 13 games in a row.

It's a tactical switch that the Blues could make this season as well under new manager Alonso, given that his Bayer Leverkusen side won the Bundesliga unbeaten in 2023-24 playing three at the back.

That incredible winning run gave Chelsea what proved to be an unassailable lead at the top of the Premier League, as they won 18 games more than in 2015-16 to win the title with 93 points.

Improving the club's points tally by a whopping 43 points again is undoubtedly a huge ask for Alonso's squad, given that it's the biggest points increase that any side has achieved to win the title in Premier League history (Leicester improved by 40 points the previous season).

But they may not need to. While Arsenal will likely mount a stronger title defence than Leicester, the Gunners' points tally last season was the second-lowest to win the Premier League since Claudio Ranieri's side 10 years ago.

The bar to become champions has dropped in the last couple of seasons from the dizzying demands of the Guardiola-Klopp era – where even 97 points wasn't enough in 2018-19 – so Chelsea might not need to reach the 93 that they achieved under Conte.

While Chelsea would still need to improve considerably to win the title, they were better than their lowly 10th-place finish last season suggests.

Based on their underlying expected goal numbers, Chelsea were the fourth-most dominant team in the Premier League (although they drop to fifth once penalties are excluded).

The problem was that Chelsea struggled to take their chances. They scored eight fewer goals than they should have, given the number and quality of shots they took – just 58 from an xG of 66.3 – with only Crystal Palace and Wolves worse finishers than them last season.

Bizarrely, the majority of that xG under-performance in front of goal came in just five games in March and April under Liam Rosenior.

Despite taking 73 shots worth 5.5 xG, the side lost five successive league games without scoring for the first time in 114 years – a run of defeats that saw Rosenior ousted as head coach.

Did Chelsea become bad finishers, was it simply a run of bad luck or was it something else? Whatever the reason, the Blues are unlikely to suffer such a sudden slump again this season.

Given where they finished, the Blues will not be playing in any European competition this campaign. While that's obviously something clubs the size of Chelsea seek to avoid, there are benefits to playing just one game a week.

Since the so-called 'Big Six' – Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Man City, Man Utd and Tottenham – all finished in the top six of the Premier League for the first time in 2010-11, nine of their sides have had no European football to play, with Chelsea and Tottenham set to join that list this season.

All but one have finished higher in the Premier League, with sides moving up five places and taking 16 more points on average than they did the previous season.

While Conte's Chelsea obviously took full advantage by winning the title, Liverpool also came very close to lifting their first Premier League trophy in 2013-14. After finishing seventh the season before, an absence of European football saw them take 23 more points but they ultimately fell just two short behind champions Manchester City.

Manchester United also took advantage of playing once a week last season by taking 29 more points than they did in 2024-25 to finish third, although there was a lot of room for improvement after finishing 15th with just 42 points the season before.

Chelsea's transformation under Antonio Conte was incredible, but there's another title-winning side that can match it – Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24.

After taking over as manager in October 2022 with the club in the relegation zone, Alonso led them to a sixth-place finish that season with 50 points – the same tally as Chelsea in both 2015-16 and last season (although Bundesliga sides play four fewer games).

Then in his first full season in charge, Leverkusen incredibly took 40 more points in 2023-24 – just three fewer than Conte's Chelsea did – to win their first-ever Bundesliga title without losing a single game.

Only two sides in Premier League history have finished outside the top three one season and won the title the next – Leicester in 2015-16 and Chelsea a year later – so the Blues repeating such a feat would be remarkable.

But with a team better than they looked last season, the benefit of no European football and a new manager that's already pulled off a miraculous transformation at one of his former clubs, it's certainly not impossible.

title: Boxer Colon dies 11 years after brain injury in fight
description: Prichard Colon, who suffered a severe brain injury during a 2015 fight, dies aged 33, his father Richard confirms on social media.
fullText:
Prichard Colon, who suffered a severe brain injury during a 2015 fight, has died aged 33, his father Richard confirmed on social media.

Colon collapsed in his changing room after the fight with Terrell Williams, during which he complained about repeated punches to the back of his head

The Puerto Rican had suffered a brain haemorraghe and after having an operation to reduce brain swelling he was placed in a coma for 221 days.

Colon lived the rest of his life in a vegetative state - unable to walk or talk - and required 24-hour care.

"Good morning, my people. I regret to inform you of the departure of my son Prichard from this earthly world," Richard Colon wrote on Facebook.

"Now he is in a better world. I did everything possible to fulfil his wish, his dream of bringing him on vacation to Puerto Rico as he so desired, but it couldn't be done.

"Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers."

Colon was undefeated in 16 fights with 13 wins by knockout before facing Williams in Fairfax, Virginia.

During the light-middleweight contest, Colon appeared to be struck in the back of the head on several occasions and Williams was deducted a point for illegal blows.

Colon was later docked two points for a low blow and was knocked down in the ninth. Believing the fight was over, Colon's corner team removed his gloves and he was disqualified.

His parents filed a lawsuit seeking more than $50m (£37m) in damages against the ringside doctor and promoters connected with the fight.

That lawsuit remains unsettled.

Colon, who was born in Florida but moved to Puerto Rico aged 10, showed great promise as a teenager and won national titles in two weight divisions.

He also boxed at the Brazil pre-Olympics with the aim of winning a spot at the 2012 Games in London, but lost in the quarter-finals and moved into the professional ranks for his debut in 2013.

"A true warrior in every sense of the word, Prichard left us with profound lessons about life, resilience, and our sport," the WBA posted on X.

In 2021, Colon was named an honorary WBC world champion by president of the sanctioning body Mauricio Sulaiman.

"Eleven years of fighting like a true champion receiving the unconditional love from your mother Nieves, your dad and so many friends who cared for Prichard Colon you will never be forgotten," Sulaiman wrote on X.

title: Swiatek answers internet critics with Toronto title
description: Iga Swiatek secures her first WTA title of the season with a straight-set victory over Elena Rybakina in the final of the Canadian Open.
fullText:
Iga Swiatek secured her first WTA title of the season with a straight-set victory over Elena Rybakina in the final of the Canadian Open on Thursday.

The six-time Grand Slam winner was cheered on by the crowd in Toronto as she beat world number two Rybakina 6-2 6-3.

Australian Open champion Rybakina struggled in the opening set and made 12 unforced errors, while Swiatek, 25, broke the Kazakhstan player's serve twice - and saved two break points of her own.

In the second set, Rybakina, 27, was unable to break world number eight Swiatek, and the Polish player clinched her 26th career title in one hour and 15 minutes.

"It means so, so much to me because the past months were not easy," said Swiatek, who will return to the top five in the rankings following her first Canadian final victory.

It has been a tough campaign for Swiatek, who will be looking to claim her first Grand Slam title since her dominant win in the Wimbledon final last year when the US Open starts later this month.

She advanced to the quarter-finals of the Australian Open in Melbourne in January but was beaten by eventual champion Rybakina. In the French Open and this year's Wimbledon, she only reached the fourth and third rounds respectively.

She appointed Spaniard Francisco Roig, who previously worked with Rafael Nadal and Emma Raducanu, to her coaching team in April.

Swiatek says it can be challenging to contend with external criticism while searching for her best form.

"I'm really happy that I kept focusing on growing, changing my game a little bit, improving despite all the opinions that many people have about me every day on the internet," said Swiatek.

"It's not easy to deal with all of that."

Rybakina led 2-1 in the second set before Swiatek won five of the final six games to end the match as champion.

Runner-up Rybakina had one ace and four double faults, hitting just 13 winners and making 23 unforced errors in total.

"I tried my best but it wasn't enough," said Rybakina, whose previous three matches went to three sets.

Meanwhile, Great Britain's Katie Boulter earned her first career win at the Cincinnati Open by defeating American Katie Volynets 7-5 0-6 6-4 in the first round.

After sealing her first victory since June, 30-year-old Boulter will face Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova in the second round.

In the men's final, fifth seed Ben Shelton secured back-to-back Canadian Open titles with a 6-3 7-6 (7-4) victory over fellow American Brandon Nakashima.

The all-American final was the first at ATP Masters 1,000 level since Andy Roddick beat Mardy Fish in Cincinnati in 2003.

Shelton is the first Canadian Open winner since Novak Djokovic in 2016 to win the tournament without dropping a set, and also the first player since Rafael Nadal in 2019 to successfully defend the title.

The 23-year-old arrived in Montreal following a disappointing run of results, suffering a first-round exit at Wimbledon, a second-round defeat at Roland Garros and managing just one win across his first four Masters 1,000 events of the season.

"To play the way that I've played this week, to go through this draw without dropping a set, I think it speaks a lot to the work that I've been putting in, but it speaks a lot to my mental toughness," Shelton said.

title: What's going on with Southampton boss Eckert's FA probe?
description: While Southampton felt the full force of the EFL's disciplionary powers at the back end of last season, Spygate is far from over with the future of Tonda Eckert still uncertain.
fullText:
While Southampton felt the full force of the EFL's disciplinary powers at the back end of last season, Spygate is far from over with the future of head coach Tonda Eckert still uncertain.

Saints' Championship campaign gets under way on Sunday and it still remains to be seen how Eckert, who was charged last month by the Football Association (FA), will be punished.

BBC Sport has been told the FA hearing is likely to be held in mid September.

Once the result is known, and with the possibility of an appeal to follow, Southampton will be a significant way into their campaign.

Eckert was charged with misconduct by the FA on 22 July for his role in the Spygate scandal that led to Saints being kicked out of the Championship play-offs in May after admitting they spied on three clubs last season.

The ongoing investigation is looking into who participated in the spying and assessing the culpability of those who knew it was happening.

BBC Sport also understands that the intern involved, Will Salt, is set to be appointed to a permanent analyst role with the club since the controversy.

Saints owner Dragan Solak revealed to BBC Sport in early June that he would not sack Eckert and that he was deserving of a second chance.

That could be taken out of his hands if the German coach is handed a lengthy ban, and it could happen in the midst of the Championship season.

The EFL opened its investigation into the spying allegations before the play-off semi-finals and charged Southampton with spying on 8 May.

Eleven days later Southampton learned their fate and were thrown out of the play-offs and given a four-point deduction for this season.

Unlike in the EFL case, which needed to be resolved in order to complete the play-offs, the FA process has allowed Southampton more time to submit evidence in support of their case.

When Southampton finally present that case it will be approaching four months after the FA began its investigation.

The Championship will pause for three weeks between Monday, 21 September to Tuesday, 6 October for the international break - but whether Southampton will learn the outcome by then is not yet known.

In short, it will depend on how long the ban is.

Eckert is only contracted at St Mary's until the end of the current season, and a significant sanction could force the club to look elsewhere for a new head coach.

Group technical director Johannes Spors provided some insight into the board's current thinking during the recent BBC Radio Solent Southampton FC fans' forum.

Spors has held his position since 2025 and played a key role in handing Eckert the permanent job as head coach in December last year.

"It all depends on what the outcome is as there are so many uncertainties of how this could look like," Spors said.

"There is nothing too concrete at the moment, we're really focused on the here and now and if there is something that we have to deal with then we will deal with it.

"In the back of my mind and in the office we do speak about different scenarios to be prepared for but I still hope for a positive outcome."

Southampton were preparing for a number of possibilities on their pre-season tour.

During one friendly Eckert watched the game from the stands, and later told the club's media: "Let's hope we don't need it," when asked about managing the game away from the technical area.

If Eckert were to be banned by the FA, there is no guarantee this would only prevent him from being on the touchline.

"At the moment I'm honestly very positive looking into the next weeks and we have some ideas in mind," Spors added.

"There was some discussions earlier about how Tonda watched one of the pre-season games from above [in the stands] and we have to think into different scenarios like this."

Throughout the Spygate process, members of the Southampton board have maintained a stance that they feel the punishment does not fit the offence committed.

Parsons echoed those feelings at last week's fans' forum but has urged the club to move on, revealing that Eckert has now been asked to "focus on football".

After initial disapointment from within the Southampton dressing room, the whole saga appears to have lit a fire inside those Saints players who missed out on playing in last season's play-off final.

Club captain Jack Stephens felt that Spygate had brought the group together, while midfielder Flynn Downes said the squad have a chip on their shoulder heading into the Championship season.

A similar mentality seems to have been adopted by some Southampton fans, who were chanting "we'll spy when we want" in their Carabao Cup opener against Colchester on Saturday.

On the other hand, some supporters raised concerns at the recent forum about season ticket prices increasing for the current campaign despite all that happened in May.

Parsons explained that the extra cost was being reinvested back into the stadium to increase the fan experience but said he appreciated people's frustrations.

While Eckert has had time to think over the summer about his actions and last season's events, the coach revealed he has been proactive during his time off, as well as cooperating with the FA's investigation.

His only prior work in senior football before the Southampton job came through 15 months as the number two at Barnsley, and three years as assistant boss at Italian club Genoa.

The 33-year-old recently revealed he had used the summer period to sharpen up his knowledge of the EFL's rules and reach out to some fellow professionals in the game.

"I've had a lot of support very quickly from the owner, sporting director and the players, but then also over the summer from lots of managers in the game, and that's helped me a lot over the summer," Eckert said in his pre-Watford news conference.

"I used the summer to not only go through the 131 rules but also to connect with some managers that have been in the game for much longer than me and managers that have much more experience than myself across national teams and club football.

"One is for the rules and regulations and the second that is even more important is the culture that's behind that, I've done that through many conversations with English managers, not just in football but other sports too."

After last weekend's 2-0 cup victory away at Colchester, Southampton start their Championship campaign at Vicarage Road on Sunday when they take on Watford.

This weekend Eckert's opposing manager will be Italian Alessio Dionisi, who he previously came up against during his time at Genoa while Dionisi was at Sassuolo.

title: 'We have to be better' - why Man City can't dwell on double
description: Manchester City have bolstered their squad this summer - but will they have enough to defend their Women's Super League crown?
fullText:
Manchester City won their first Women's Super League title in a decade last season, adding the Women's FA Cup trophy to their cabinet for good measure.

However, with Arsenal strengthening this summer and Chelsea hoping to bounce back after a disappointing campaign, can City stay at the top in 2026-27?

City are also being chased by ambitious clubs lower down the table as London City Lionesses and Tottenham have made waves in the transfer market and Brighton have been on the rise under manager Dario Vidosic.

City have bolstered their squad with the additions of England internationals Beth Mead and Niamh Charles - but will they have enough to defend their crown?

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

What are the key dates for the women's football season?

City were crowned champions with a game to spare and a six-point gap to second-placed Chelsea last season.

It ended Chelsea's six-year dominance and was City's first major trophy under manager Andree Jeglertz in his debut campaign in England.

No Champions League football, a squad stacked with quality and the ability to keep key players fit proved vital - but what did the players learn?

"How to become champions," captain Alex Greenwood told BBC Sport.

"We had come very, very close to doing it in previous years but just couldn't get over the line. Last season, a lot came together."

There will be new challenges this season as City return to European football meaning a busier fixture schedule.

The squad will be tested more, though they were boosted by top-scorer Khadija Shaw's decision to sign a new contract, avoiding a potential switch to Chelsea.

The arrivals of England duo Mead and Charles has added depth but City lost Brazilian forward Kerolin to Barcelona.

Elsewhere, Spain full-back Ona Batlle and England midfielder Georgia Stanway have joined Arsenal, London City Lionesses have signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and Tottenham have improved their frontline with the additions of Kirsty Hanson and Shekiera Martinez.

But Greenwood is not fazed by others and says the message to her team-mates remains the same, though they need to keep improving.

"Continuity is important, culture is important and the language that you use is important. When you hear the same thing often, it becomes a norm," she added.

"You act like a champion and perform like one. We all locked into that last year and were fully committed.

"This season, I'm not going to say 'do the same again' because I don't think that entitles you to win the league. People improve, teams improve and we will improve.

"We will have to change things slightly and be better but continue to do the things that we did really well last season. That would be my message... and to enjoy it."

Inside Man City's WSL title-winning season

Unmasking the coach plotting Man City's quest for a domestic double

Investment at clubs outside the WSL's top four makes for an exciting season ahead with deeper competition across the league.

City will have to be wary of their traditional rivals, but also of clubs looking to upset the usual order such as London City Lionesses, Tottenham and Brighton.

However, Greenwood does not think they need to be looking over their shoulders.

"I think the reaction is from the teams who have tried to get into the top four and haven't quite got there," said Greenwood.

"It's amazing though. I love seeing players come to this league and want to test themselves. In my opinion, it's the best league in the world in women's football.

"I don't think any game you play in the WSL is easy. We'll see when the season starts how things look. I concentrate on this team and where I'm at."

It is another big year for Greenwood, who is hoping to help England go far at the Women's World Cup in Brazil next summer.

She is used to the big stage having won back-to-back European titles with the Lionesses but Greenwood says lifting the WSL trophy as captain taught her things.

"It was those big moments of pressure - I was interested to see how I would handle those situations," she added.

"I've been in winning teams where we've won trophies but I was captain last season so it did feel a little bit different in terms of responsibility.

"I really enjoyed it. I tried to embrace it as much as I could. I relied on people to help me in situations where I felt I needed it and I don't think that's a bad thing.

"I'm not perfect and I don't have all the answers just because I wear the armband. I did learn a lot about myself. I learned to enjoy it along the way too because it gets tense!"

title: Hasan hits Bangladesh's first century in Australia
description: Tanzid Hasan Tamim becomes the first Bangladesh cricketer to score a Test century in Australia as the visitors continued to dominate on day two in Darwin.
fullText:
First Test, Darwin (day two of five)

Australia 198: Smith 71; Mahmud 6-55

Bangladesh 351-6: Tanzid 101, Shanto 84, Mominul 49

Tanzid Hasan Tamim became the first Bangladesh cricketer to score a Test century in Australia as the visitors continued to dominate on day two in Darwin.

The opener, playing in just his second Test match, hit 101 off 197 balls as Bangladesh closed on 351-6, a lead of 153.

"I can't describe it in words, but it was very special for me," he said. "I love to play in these conditions, the pitch is getting better and better."

Hasan began the day on 32 with Bangladesh 96-1, having bowled Australia out for 198 on day one after the hosts won the toss.

The 25-year-old put on 102 for the second wicket with Mominul Haque, who was dismissed by Josh Hazlewood for 49 before lunch.

Tanzid then put on 93 with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto as Australia toiled in stiflingly hot conditions at the Marrara Oval.

His innings finally came to an end when he drove a Nathan Lyon delivery to Mitchell Starc at long-off during the afternoon session.

Australia rallied with three quick wickets with the new ball after tea, but Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Hasan Mahmud put on an unbeaten 43 before stumps to keep Bangladesh on top.

Australia have never lost a home Test to Bangladesh, only losing once to the Tigers in six previous Tests - at Mirpur in 2017.

This is the first of a two-Test series.

title: Arsenal express interest in signing Quansah
description: Arsenal express an interest in signing Bayer Leverkusen and England defender Jarell Quansah.
fullText:
Arsenal have expressed an interest in signing Bayer Leverkusen defender Jarell Quansah.

BBC Sport understands that talks are at an exploratory stage at the moment but sources suggest a deal for the 23-year-old is possible.

The potential move comes after the Gunners held further talks over a transfer for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa.

Villa want a fee of around £60m for Konsa but Arsenal value the 28-year-old closer to £40m.

Quansah would fit the profile of player that the Gunners are looking for, as he can play at both centre-back and right-back.

But it remains to be seen if their interest in the former Liverpool defender is a tactic by the club in their pursuit of Quansah's England team-mate Konsa.

Fresh talks over Arsenal move for Aston Villa's Konsa

Arsenal will be without William Saliba for the start of their Premier League title defence next weekend against promoted Coventry City, as the France centre-back has been ruled out for an extended period after suffering a back injury at the World Cup.

Netherlands right-back Jurrien Timber, who missed two months towards the end of last season because of an ankle injury, is also struggling to be fit.

Liverpool have the option to match any offer for Quansah as part of the deal that led to him leaving Anfield for the Bundesliga club last year, but it is understood they have no intention of actioning their clause.

Quansah was part of the England squad that reached the semi-finals of the World Cup this summer.

He started three games at the tournament at right-back, but he was sent off in the last-16 match against Mexico, forcing him to miss the quarter-final win over Norway and last-four defeat by Argentina.

Quansah made 44 appearances for Leverkusen last season, scoring five goals.

title: European Cup winner Rimmer dies aged 78
description: European Cup winner and former Aston Villa and Manchester United goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer dies at the age of 78.
fullText:
European Cup winner and former Aston Villa and Manchester United goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has died at the age of 78.

The Southport-born goalkeeper was on the bench when United beat Benfica to win the 1968 European Cup.

Rimmer started Villa's 1-0 win over Bayern Munich in the 1982 European Cup final, though he was replaced by Nigel Spink after nine minutes because of a neck injury.

He started every game of Villa's run to the final, as he did in their league title-winning campaign of 1980-81.

Rimmer made 229 league appearances for the Midlands club, and also spent time with Swansea City and Arsenal. He won the latter's player of the season award in 1974-75.

Rimmer earned one England cap in a friendly against Italy in 1976.

Aston Villa and Manchester United both said they were "deeply saddened" by Rimmer's death, while Arsenal also paid tribute.

Rimmer's former United team-mate Alex Stepney, a fellow goalkeeper, said on social media: "Such sad news to hear Jimmy Rimmer has passed away, rest in peace and lots of love to Jimmy's family x."

fullText:
The sports front pages for August 14, 2026 are dominated by the imminent transfer of Ferran Torres to PSG for 50 million, the Rodri saga between Barça and Manchester City, the start of the league season, and the latest transfer market moves.

Marca devotes its front page to the start of the league season under the slogan "The best league in the world is back / Where champions are made". fullText:
The summer transfer market is entering its most frantic phase, with astronomical moves among Europe's football giants. From the imminent agreement between FC Barcelona and PSG for Ferran Torres to Cristian 'Cuti' Romero's triumphant arrival in the Spanish capital, the sports headlines this August 13 are packed with plot twists, multimillion-euro deals, and institutional decisions that will shape the 2026/27 season calendar.

FC Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain have reached a final agreement for the transfer of Ferran Torres for a fee close to €50 million. The Valencia-born forward is set to head to the French capital to immediately join Luis Enrique's squad, in a strategic deal that allows the Blaugrana club to free up significant room within its financial fair play limits.

Rodrigo Hernández is already back in Manchester. The international midfielder rejoins Manchester City training today under Enzo Maresca, while his future remains completely up in the air. Barcelona continue to put intense pressure on the English club to complete his signing, in one of the most complex negotiations of the current summer window.

The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) officially announced that the 2027 Spanish Super Cup will change venue. The first title of the season will be contested in Istanbul (Turkey) from February 2 to 7, an organizational decision prompted by the tournament's clash with the Asian Cup being held in Arab territory.

A decisive day for the Atlético de Madrid defense. Cristian 'Cuti' Romero landed in the Spanish capital last night from Córdoba. The Argentine center-back will undergo his medical early this Friday and, if everything goes according to plan, will sign his contract to formally become the new leader of Diego Simeone's back line.

A historic deal in the youth ranks of Real Madrid. Forward Jacobo Ortega, registered with the C team and without ever making his first-team debut, is finalizing his move to French side Strasbourg in exchange for €10 million for 70% of his rights. Elche fought for the signing until the very last moment, but the French offer ultimately tipped the balance.

title: Real Madrid midfield still searching for rhythm; transfer move could now depend on key condition
description: Real Madrid’s midfield situation remains one of the key talking points this transfer window, but the club may be forced to stand still unless there is a change within the current squad.According to ...
fullText:
Real Madrid's midfield situation remains one of the key talking points this transfer window, but the club may be forced to stand still unless there is a change within the current squad.

According to El Larguero, Real Madrid are not entirely satisfied with how their midfield is functioning, with the current group still struggling to find the right rhythm.

However, any new move in the market appears dependent on the club creating space first.

Notably, Jose Mourinho had already made his desire for a more creative midfielder clear during his first discussions with the club.

Real Madrid responded by bringing in Bernardo Silva, giving the Portuguese manager an experienced option.

Yet despite that signing, the midfield has not fully clicked, and the issue is said to be similar to one the team faced last season.

No Real Madrid player wants to leave this summer. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

The club's current position is to focus on getting more from the midfielders already available rather than immediately entering the market for another major signing.

Real Madrid have considered strengthening the area further, with Rodri emerging as one of the names linked with the club.

However, the Manchester City midfielder has decided to move to Barcelona instead.

Hence, the preference is either to improve the performances and understanding of the players already at Mourinho's disposal or to take advantage of an opportunity in the transfer market if the right player becomes available on suitable terms.

That leaves Real Madrid in a waiting game, as only a departure from the current squad would make it easier for the club to consider another arrival.

At present, though, that possibility appears complicated because none of the midfielders are actively looking to leave before the transfer window closes.

Real Madrid midfielders are not clicking. (Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images)

This is where Real Madrid's transfer plans become difficult.

The club has limited room to bring in another midfielder without first changing the balance of the squad.

As such, only a sale or departure would help create that space, but no player currently appears interested in forcing an exit.

As a result, Real Madrid could enter the final part of the transfer window without making another midfield signing, even though there are concerns about the performances of the current group.

The situation could still change if a suitable offer arrives for one of the players or if a member of the squad decides to leave. Until then, however, the club have little reason to make a major move.

title: Man City to sell Tijjani Reijnders in £50m deal just a year after joining
description: Reijnders joined from AC Milan last summer for £46.5m but fell out of favour towards the end of City’s season
fullText:
Manchester City are set to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah after agreeing a £51m deal.

The midfielder has accepted personal terms with the Saudi Arabian club as he will leave the Etihad Stadium after just a year.

City, whose midfield overhaul is continuing, will make a profit on Reijnders, who cost £46.5m when he joined from AC Milan last summer.

And his departure will mean they have brought in around £100m in transfer fees this window, with Nathan Ake's sale to Fenerbahce and James Trafford's move to Leeds.

Reijnders, who had also attracted interest from Nottingham Forest, scored seven goals in 50 games for City.

But he lost his place last season, with former manager Pep Guardiola preferring to pair captain Bernardo Silva with Rodri.

And while Silva is gone and Rodri, who is a target for Barcelona, could follow, City have signed Elliot Anderson from Forest for £116m.

They are also interested in other midfielders, including Morocco's Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, and could put the fee from Reijnders towards a replacement.

title: Rising golf star, 18, dies after brain haemorrhage
description: Promising Australian golfer Jessica Bang dies at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage as she prepared for a tournament in Thailand.
fullText:
Jessica Bang, a promising Australian golfer, has died at the age of 18 after suffering a brain haemorrhage.

Bang, who won her first professional event in just her fifth start earlier this year, was preparing for a tournament in Thailand on 1 August when she collapsed.

She was rushed to a hospital in Bangkok and had emergency brain surgery. After being in intensive care for nearly two weeks, she died on Thursday.

The WPGA Tour of Australasia said Bang, who turned professional at the end of 2025, was an "outstanding young talent".

"The thoughts and prayers of everyone at the WPGA Tour of Australasia and the broader Australian golf community are with Jessica's family, friends and all those who knew and loved her at this incredibly difficult time," a statement read.

Writing on a GoFundMe page that was set up by Bang's cousins after her collapse, family members said: "We are truly heartbroken by this news.

"The funds we have raised will be given to her parents to help contribute towards her medical expenses."

Bang recently qualified to start her rookie season in the WPGA, having won the Queensland Amateur in 2025.

She shot a final-round 65 to win a regional qualifying event in February to reach the NWS Women's Open on the Ladies European Tour, where she missed the cut.

title: WinCore – Open-Source Windows Utilities for AI and PyTorch
description: WinCode Library. Contribute to FWKMultiverse/WinCore development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Windows-focused utilities for reliable Python and PyTorch workflows.

WinCore is a free and open-source Python library designed specifically to address
common development and machine-learning workflow problems on Windows.

It provides practical utilities for system inspection, CPU and memory management,
PyTorch compilation and precision handling, GPU monitoring, diagnostics,
multi-GPU workflows, caching, and Windows-aware I/O.

PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/WinCore/0.6.3/

WinCore is designed to be practical and conservative. When hardware or
environment information cannot be reliably detected, it prefers reporting
unknown or falling back safely rather than inventing results.

This README provides the project overview and quick-start information.

For the complete public API, including functions, classes, parameters,
return values, and behavior, see the full API Reference:

The API Reference contains the detailed technical documentation for WinCore
and should be used when integrating or working with a specific API.

WinCore 0.6.3 is the first full public release of the project.

The library is publicly available for general use. However, comprehensive
testing across every supported Windows configuration, hardware combination,
GPU, driver, Python version, and PyTorch version has not yet been completed.

Some behavior may therefore vary between environments.

If you encounter unexpected behavior, compatibility issues, or incorrect
results, please report them through the project's issue tracker:

https://github.com/FWKMultiverse/WinCore/issues

Bug reports, reproducible examples, and environment information are especially
helpful for improving compatibility and reliability.

You are free to use, copy, modify, distribute, sublicense, and incorporate
WinCore into your own projects, subject to the terms of the MIT License.

title: Private security firms will soon be allowed to hack overseas cybercriminals
description: Trump memo is first time gov't has authorized private sector to perform cyberattacks.
fullText:
The Trump administration is recruiting private security firms to conduct federal government-authorized operations, including cyberattacks, against overseas-based criminal organizations that commit hacks on US persons, organizations, or government entities.

In a National Security Presidential Memorandum issued Thursday, US President Donald Trump directed the National Coordination Center (NCC), which operates under the Homeland Security Task Force, to develop a program for conducting specific cyber operations that combat foreign transnational criminal organizations (TCOs). The Departments of Justice and Homeland Security will provide oversight. The lynchpin of that program is bringing in private sector companies to participate.

A fact sheet that accompanied Thursday’s memo listed ransomware, sextortion schemes, phishing campaigns, financial fraud, and impersonation scams as activities eligible for private-sector security firms to target. The memo said such firms could “conduct Cyber Surveillance Operations and Cyber Effects Operations” against “cyber-enabled” TCOs. Such groups are defined as “any foreign group that conducts cyber-enabled crime against the United States Government, a United States person, or United States interests, and that is not an institutional part of a foreign government or wholly operated under a foreign government’s direction.”

The new program is the first time the federal government will authorize private companies to conduct offensive cyber operations against overseas hackers. The memo appears to permit companies participating in the program to use spyware or launch offensive attacks intended to destroy TCO data or systems. The memo doesn’t rule out certain types of offensive attacks, such as those that use encryption to lock targets out of their networks or performing distributed denial-of-service attacks. Up until now, the government has prohibited the private sector from taking such actions without court-authorized approval.

“There’s definitely merit in the idea of hacking ransomware groups and it does already in fact happen (don’t ask me how I know),” independent security researcher Kevin Beamont said in response to the memo. “But the correct incentives have gotta be there.”

He added: “The biggest problem I’ve had with fighting ransomware over the past 5 years is private cyber companies basically lobbying for nothing to change. A lot of companies have made a lot of money, so putting them in charge of stopping it seems optimistic.”

The memo placed specific limits on the scope of the new program. Private companies must first be approved after vetting by the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security. Cyber Effects Operations and Cyber Surveillance Operations may not result in “Critical Outcomes,” meaning those that result in the loss of life or serious injury or “rise to the level of use of force or armed attack under international law.” The memo also notes:

[M]inimum standards that Participating Companies must meet in order to take part in the Program, which shall include appropriate levels of technical proficiency, proven performance of cyber operations, facility security, personnel vetting, competence, reliability, and other factors that the Program Executive Directors, in coordination with the Homeland Security Council, determine are relevant or necessary for guaranteeing high confidence in a Participating Company’s ability to perform successfully.

Participating companies must also deposit $1 million in an escrow account. The deposit will be forfeited “should the Participating Company enter non‑compliance with its contractual agreement described” in the memo.

Many of the specifics of the policy remain undefined. These details will be crucial to determining how effective and judicious the program will be. The memo directs the Justice and Homeland Security departments to deliver the particulars in the next 60 days.

title: Man who carried Clinton nuclear 'football' reveals what 'scares the hell out of me' about Air Force One story
description: Retired Air Force Lt. Col. Robert Patterson said he suspects a "highly placed" leaker revealed the story of President Donald Trump's Air Force One swap.
fullText:
A retired Air Force lieutenant colonel who carried the nuclear "football" for former President Bill Clinton says the extraordinary Air Force One shell game departing Ankara, Turkey, last month to protect President Donald Trump from a potential attack was hardly unprecedented.

"It was brilliant," retired Lt. Col. Robert "Buzz" Patterson told Fox News Digital. "I wish I had been a part of it. That's how well done it was."

But Patterson is warning that exposing the vital national security secrets behind such operations could put presidents, military personnel and the White House press corps in danger for years to come.

Patterson served as Clinton's senior military aide for a period of two years and was responsible for the president's emergency satchel, and in a 20-minute interview Wednesday, he explained how presidential decoys, aircraft swaps and other acts of deception are longstanding tools used to protect the commander in chief, his senior officials and the "privileged" Air Force One press corps.

Trump Used Catering Truck, Air Force One Decoy To Evade Iran Threat: Report

What alarms him, Patterson said, is not that Trump's security team used the tactic — including the catering truck sleight of hand he was intimately a part of during the Clinton administration — but that details of how it was done are now spilling into public view.

"I hope that they prosecute this to the fullest," Patterson said. "Whoever leaked that, in my opinion, and having been involved in this, was highly placed in that process."

"There's only a few people who actually know exactly what's going down, and that's by design," he added. "So if somebody leaked it, it was somebody involved in the process, and that scares the hell out of me."

'Decoy' Air Force One Was Protected By Us Fighter Jets, Official Says

His warning comes as Fox News reported Wednesday that the legacy presidential 747 used as a decoy after Trump secretly switched planes in Ankara, Turkey, last month was not sent into the sky unprotected.

A senior Trump administration official told Fox News that U.S. fighter jets protected the aircraft on its flight to the United Kingdom. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were also aboard with members of the traveling press corps, according to the official. Reporters had been instructed to keep their window shades closed.

Patterson said the fighter escort was exactly the sort of protection he would expect in a high-threat environment.

Trump Says He's Iran's 'No. 1' Target As Renewed Conflict Raises Assassination Fears

"Yes, especially into war zones," Patterson said, when asked whether presidential aircraft are customarily escorted by fighter jets in such circumstances.

"We damn sure always do when we're going to a theater of high threat," he said. "We did it with President Clinton in '97. And we did it with Trump just a couple weeks ago, and we'll do it with whoever the next president is."

Trump's Sly Plane Switch Raises Eyebrows Over Safety Of Passengers Left Behind On Board

Trump's July 8 departure from the NATO summit in Ankara involved a carefully staged deception.

Trump publicly boarded the familiar blue-and-white presidential 747 before being moved out of sight in an airport catering vehicle and transferred to a smaller Air Force C-32A. The legacy 747 then departed for Britain while Trump traveled separately. He later reunited with the presidential aircraft in the United Kingdom before continuing his journey aboard the newer, Qatari-donated 747.

Trump said Tuesday that he was following the direction of the Secret Service and the military.

Patterson said the broader concept of confusing potential attackers about the president's movements is routine.

White House Pushed For Protocol To Preserve Correspondents' Credibility After Trump's Secret Plane Switch

"We use decoys all the time," he said. "We use decoy in the motorcade routes."

"You'll sometimes see the two beasts will switch out under bridges and overpasses. We do the same thing with airplanes, especially in international trips. There's always two Air Force Ones that go. Obviously, one's a decoy and it's also a spare for spare parts in case something happens to the primary.

"So we've been doing it for years.

"It works," he added, "and for people to want to have visibility into actually how it works would be particularly troubling and it would cause reverberations in our American system for years."

Secret Service Agent On Jd Vance's Detail Investigated For Allegedly Leaking Operational Security Info

That is why, he argued, demands to expose the mechanics of the latest operation risk doing more damage than the public scrutiny is worth.

Patterson said the protections are intended not merely for Trump, Clinton or any individual president, but to ensure continuity of the presidency itself.

"President Trump's only got two more years," he said. "These programs are going to be in place for the foreseeable future, and they've been in place in our past for quite a while. So it's not just about Trump. These programs exist to protect no matter who the president is and the team around him."

Patterson, who is a conservative and outspoken New York Times bestselling author highly critical of the man he carried the nuclear football for, warned divisive politics against Trump is dangerous for U.S. national security.

Two Years After Butler, Threats Against Trump Keep Assassination Attempt In Sharp Focus

"Like I was with President Clinton — I wasn't a huge President Clinton fan, but they hired me into that position, the White House did — and I swore an oath to the office of the presidency, and I did it," Patterson said. "And I think that the people that are working for President Trump right now, whether they like him or don't like him, or agree with his politics or don't agree with this politics, they have to understand that we're there — the Secret Service guys, the apparatus is there — to protect the human being and the office."

Patterson also revealed that Trump was not the first president he knew of to use an airport catering vehicle as part of a clandestine movement: "As far as I know, President Clinton was the first one to do it."

Decades before Trump was moved between aircraft in Ankara, Patterson said a catering truck was used to discreetly move Clinton aboard a presidential aircraft during an episode that was never publicly reported at the time.

"I won't go into a lot of detail, but, President Clinton was incapable of going up the front steps," he said. "So we used a catering truck to get them onto the back of the airplane, unbeknownst to anybody else that was there except for a few of us. And we never told anybody and nobody ever reported it."

Trump Has Become America's Most Targeted Leader, Facing Threats Every Few Months

"And we flew back to D.C. kind of unannounced. And we've done it before. I was on with President Clinton in 1997 when we did the surprise visit to Bosnia. So he went to Bosnia on Christmas Eve to surprise the troops. So we didn't tell anybody then. I was all on that trip the entire way, 36 hours nonstop that day. And we didn't tell anybody, and the press didn't know, and they never complained about it.

"And it was important. We wanted to get President Clinton into a war zone without anybody else knowing about it. And that's kind of what was happening to Trump. They wanted to him out of a potential war zone, without anybody knowing about it.

"We do it all the time. It's safe, it's reliable, and the public does not need to know."

Past presidents have repeatedly used secrecy and deception for travel into dangerous areas. Clinton used decoy aircraft during a 2000 trip to Pakistan, while subsequent presidents have made covert or tightly held trips to Iraq, Afghanistan and Ukraine. The precise circumstances and level of knowledge afforded to traveling reporters have differed between administrations.

Patterson pushed back against criticism that Trump's operation improperly endangered the reporters and officials who continued aboard the legacy presidential aircraft.

He noted that the aircraft was carrying not only journalists but an Air Force crew and senior government officials — and, as Fox News has now reported, was protected by fighter aircraft.

"We're not going to put those people at risk either," Patterson said flatly of the Air Force personnel.

He argued that some of the media criticism has lost sight of the wider security apparatus involved in presidential travel.

"A lot of what is being spouted on social media and in our mainstream media is factually incorrect," Patterson said, "and it's actually troubling because it's going to endanger not only President Trump, but future presidents to come."

Patterson called efforts to expose the procedures "incredibly dangerous" and "irresponsible."

The danger, he said, extends beyond the president.

"It endangers everybody in the process — Secret Service guys, military aide guys, Air Force guys that are on alert, Army guys that are on alert," Patterson said.

The retired officer said presidential protection plans are deliberately compartmentalized so that very few people know the full operation.

That is what makes the source of the disclosures particularly concerning to him.

Patterson warned there could also be a longer-term cost to revealing too much about presidential deception tactics: Future commanders in chief could lose the ability to make surprise visits to troops or enter high-threat regions at all.

If the tactics become predictable, he argued, planners would have to devise entirely new security procedures.

"If we were to expose everything, we would have to overhaul the entire security apparatus of the United States of America," Patterson said, warning that doing so could put "the presidency and the Cabinet members in incredible danger."

Asked whether overexposing such programs could effectively prevent Trump or future presidents from making some high-risk overseas trips, Patterson agreed.

For Patterson, that makes the argument over the Trump flight bigger than one president, one press corps or one flight out of Turkey.

The tactics being publicly dissected today, he warned, may be the same ones needed to save a future president — and everyone traveling with that president — tomorrow.

"We just need to leave them alone," Patterson said.

Original article

title: The 3 things student-loan borrowers told us are confusing them the most right now
description: Student-loan borrowers are facing sweeping repayment changes. Here's what's on their minds, from new payments to billing errors.
fullText:
Student-loan borrowers are navigating a host of repayment changes.

The changes are a result of Trump's repayment overhaul, which took effect July 1.

Borrowers have reported inaccurate bills and payment glitches, sparking confusion.

What's confusing you about your student loans?

Over the past year, Business Insider has heard from over 1,000 student-loan borrowers who described challenges, concerns, and confusion related to President Donald Trump's student-loan repayment changes.

The changes, which included new repayment plans and borrowing caps, took effect July 1. The transition, however, has not been seamless — borrowers have faced incorrect bills, confusing servicer notices, and paperwork backlogs that have made it difficult to budget their lives.

Here are some of the key things student-loan borrowers have expressed confusion over in the new repayment environment.

President Donald Trump eliminated the Biden-era SAVE plan in March. It would have allowed for cheaper payments and a shorter timeline to debt relief. Beginning July 1, servicers started notifying SAVE borrowers of their 90-day timeframe to transition to a new plan. If they do not take action within that timeframe, they will be automatically placed on the standard, most expensive plan.

Many student-loan borrowers on SAVE have reported confusion with the process. Prior to July 1, the Department of Education notified borrowers that they would soon have to switch plans and encouraged them to do so as early as possible.

Borrowers said the notification process from the department and servicers has been confusing. For example, some borrowers said they switched plans before receiving their 90-day timeframe, as encouraged by the department, and didn't have time to appropriately budget for their new, higher payments.

Other borrowers are still waiting to receive their notices. Servicers are notifying borrowers in waves and expect to send all notices out by the end of 2026, with the earliest deadline to transition off SAVE coming at the end of September. It's unclear how quickly borrowers who did not take action will be placed in the standard plan, and there's an ongoing lawsuit seeking to stop the involuntary transfer.

Over the past few months, borrowers have reported erroneous notices and billing errors that have made it difficult to understand their current repayment status.

In June, the Education Department confirmed to Business Insider that borrowers who shared their federal tax information with Federal Student Aid received incorrect $50 payments. A month later, 6,000 of those borrowers received emails requiring them to reapply for an income-driven repayment plan.

More recently, borrowers reported receiving notices from their servicer indicating their loans were past due, though that wasn't the case. The department said that the issue has been fixed and that affected borrowers would be notified.

Those glitches, and others, have sparked panic and confusion among borrowers. Some said they weren't aware the glitches were errors until they read about them in the news or on social media, and that they had budgeted their lives based on the incorrect billing information they received.

Trump's repayment overhaul included a new $100,000 lifetime borrowing cap for graduate programs, and a $200,000 cap for professional programs. It also placed new limits on the amount parents can borrow for their kids: a $20,000 annual cap and a $65,000 lifetime cap per student. Parents had previously been able to borrow the full cost of attendance.

In addition to the new caps, the Trump administration planned to implement a new definition of a professional degree, which would allow 11 programs to qualify for the higher borrowing limit and exclude many others, including advanced nursing. A court blocked the new definition from taking effect, and while the prior definition now remains in place, it could change as the litigation continues.

Borrowers said the uncertainty surrounding how much they can borrow is weighing on their future financial and educational planning. Some borrowers said they anticipate having to forgo their programs if they do not get sufficient federal funding. Parents also said they're concerned about supporting their kids' education under the new limits.

Have a story to share about student loans? Contact this reporter at asheffey@businessinsider.com.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

title: Fury erupts as 37-year illegal alien demands citizenship in viral Spanish rant alongside Dem leaders
description: A viral video clip shows an illegal alien demanding amnesty in Spanish alongside Democratic Party leaders, sparking fierce backlash over immigration laws.
fullText:
Furious users took to social media to blast an illegal alien who has been present in the United States for 37 years after she demanded amnesty in a Spanish rant alongside top Democratic Party leaders.

"I ask that you be champions of a change in the immigration laws," said Margarita Cielo Balbuena, flanked by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and Rep. Rob Menendez, D-N.J., through an interpreter earlier this week.

"We need a path to citizenship for those of us that have been present for at least seven years in this country," she continued. "We need a stop to these raids that immigration is using to terrorize Dover [New Jersey]."

Illegal Immigrant Top Dem Fought To Free Turns Up On Voter Rolls: 'Mockery Of Our Immigration Laws'

A clip of the video went viral online Wednesday.

"It is not just that someone like me, who has been in this country since 1989, who pays taxes, who is a homeowner, who is a business owner who gives work to others, someone who has children and grandchildren who are born in this country — that I have to suffer the psychological and physical abuse and that I also have to suffer the humiliation that is the violent arrest and detention in a detention center," said Cielo Balbuena.

The foreign-born woman was detained in ICE's Elizabeth Detention Center for two months, and claimed that she was treated inhumanely, according to the New Jersey Globe.

But online opponents of illegal immigration were not sympathetic to Cielo Balbuena's call.

Illegal Immigrant Who Murdered Michigan Woman Sues Trump, Demands $75M, Public Apology, Us Citizenship

Among her most prominent and harshest critics was former U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) commander-at-large Gregory Bovino.

"You have lived in the United States since 1989. That is 37 years. You still need a translator," he listed.

"At a Democratic event you stood up and demanded a path to citizenship for anyone who has been here just 7 years," Bovino continued. "Notice the arrogance. Notice the entitlement."

He went on to claim that Democrats' open borders policies allowed so many foreigners into the country so quickly that "assimilation is no longer required."

"There can be no amnesty and there can be no exceptions. All illegals must go," the John Birch Society said on X in response to the video.

Democrat Compares Ice To 'Domestic Terrorists' As 111 House Dems Demand Texas Detention Center Close

"No English. No citizenship," said popular online personality Brigitte Gabriel.

"No. Someone who wanted to be a citizen would care enough to learn the language. In any country," said another post that garnered over 1,000 likes.

"Immediate deportation," said actor Matthew Marsden. "A just country that cares about its citizens should defend it. That includes getting rid of people like this."

Rep. Jeffries spoke at the event, and demanded the closure of Delaney Hall, another ICE detention facility in New Jersey that was subject to intense protests and sometimes violent riots for months earlier this year.

Georgia Ice Sweep Nabs Over 700 Criminal Illegal Aliens, Including Sex Offenders, Child Abusers

"Delaney Hall needs to be shut down," Jeffries said. "That will remain a high priority for us until it takes place."

"The behavior that ICE is engaging in is inconsistent with our values and what America should represent."

The White House fired back in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying: "These types of smears by sanctuary politicians are contributing to our ICE law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them and an 8,000% increase in death threats."

"Our ICE officers are heroes who put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists from American communities. Democrats must stop demonizing our officers for simply enforcing our nation's laws," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said.

fullText:
(Bloomberg) -- Shein Global Holdings Ltd. plans to start taking investor orders for its long-awaited Hong Kong initial public offering as soon as Aug. 20 and debut in the city around Aug. 28, according to people familiar with the matter.

Walter Sells Lakers, Seeks More Cash to Pay Loans Amid DOJ Probe

Shein had been targeting a valuation of about $30 billion in the IPO — a fraction of its peak — but has faced pushback from investors and may lower it further, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private information. Existing shareholders may take up as much as about half of the deal, they said.

The fast-fashion retailer is gauging demand for the offering, which is likely to raise $2 billion to $3 billion, Bloomberg News reported last week.

Deliberations are ongoing and details such as size, valuation and timing may change, the people said.

Closely held Shein is nearing the end of a long journey to go public, after failing to proceed with IPOs in both New York and London. After reaching about $100 billion, its valuation has plummeted as growth slowed due to factors such as tariffs and competition from PDD Holdings Inc.'s Temu.

Shein has told prospective investors it expects net income to drop this year and then return to nearer last year's $2.06 billion in 2027, some of the people said.

Shein is trying to position itself as a peer to Zara owner Inditex SA or H&M AB, which have price-to-earnings ratios of 28.7 and 19.5, respectively. Morgan Stanley expects the company's 2025-2028 net profit growth rate to be higher than Inditex's and H&M's.

Shein didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Founded in mainland China and now headquartered in Singapore, Shein built a global fast-fashion empire by offering low-priced, trend-driven apparel shipped directly from suppliers. But US tariffs followed by war in the Middle East have pushed up material costs and prices for consumers.

title: Iran to join BRICS development bank soon, central bank governor says
description: Iran will soon join the New Development Bank, the development lender established by the BRICS group of nations, central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati said in a state media
fullText:
DUBAI, Aug 13 (Reuters) - Iran will soon join the New Development Bank, the development lender established by the BRICS group of nations, ‌central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati said in a state media report published ‌on Wednesday ahead of a BRICS finance meeting in India.

Iran remains under sweeping U.S. and international ​sanctions, and it has yet to reach a peace deal to end the current conflict with the U.S. and Israel, giving Tehran added incentive to seek alternative financial channels outside the dollar system.

The NDB's corporate communications division told Reuters it ‌could not confirm information regarding ⁠Iran's membership.

Iran joined BRICS in 2024 as the group expanded, in a move aimed at deepening economic ties among emerging ⁠economies, and it has since made clear its desire to become a member and shareholder of the NDB.

The bank was set up by Brazil, Russia, India, China and ​South ​Africa in 2015 to finance infrastructure and ​sustainable development projects. It has since ‌expanded its membership to include the United Arab Emirates, Egypt and other emerging economies.

"The most important result of cooperation among BRICS member countries is the establishment of the New Development Bank, and our country will soon become a member of this bank," Hemmati said, according to state media.

Hemmati is attending the first ‌meeting of BRICS finance ministers and central ​bank governors, hosted by India, which holds the ​rotating BRICS chairmanship this year.

BRICS ​members have sought to reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar ‌by promoting trade and financial transactions in ​national currencies.

Hemmati said ​Iran believed BRICS members could conduct trade using their national currencies and was seeking bilateral and trilateral monetary cooperation with other members.

NDB membership is ​open to members of ‌the United Nations, as well as to borrowing and non-borrowing member ​countries, the bank said. Uzbekistan became its 10th member on June 5.

(Reporting ​by Dubai Newsroom; Editing by Hugh Lawson)

title: Stacey Abrams tells nodding Kamala Harris that southerners have lived under 'soft authoritarianism' since 1776
description: Stacey Abrams told Kamala Harris on her podcast that the American South represents what authoritarianism looks like in the U.S., dating back to 1776.
fullText:
Georgia Democrat Stacey Abrams suggested to a nodding former Vice President Kamala Harris during an interview Thursday that the American South is what the United States looks like as an authoritarian country.

On her "Assembly Required" podcast, Abrams, who ran unsuccessfully twice for governor of Georgia, spoke to Harris about the future of the Democratic Party and the challenges it faces, particularly in southern states.

"I grew up in Mississippi, came of age in Georgia, and I know you've been spending a lot of time in the South recently. You've been to Tennessee and Louisiana and North Carolina," Abrams told Harris. "And what I tell people when they want to understand what authoritarianism can look like in the U.S., I say, 'Look South.' We have lived under soft authoritarianism, I would say, since, oh, 1776."

"And what it has meant is that we have seen the warning signs long before the rest of the country, but we've also been the architects of the solutions long before the rest of the country understands it," she continued.

Blockbuster Supreme Court Voting Rights Ruling Ignites Redistricting War Across Southern States

She went on to claim that the American debate about voter ID is fake.

"And when you talk about what's happening in North Carolina, I liken it to the fact that we are having this false debate about voter ID. Every state requires that you identify who you are. But if you're in Texas, you can use your gun license and not your student ID," she said. "If you're in North Carolina, yeah, you can vote if you can manage to get to a polling place where, you know, a lot of students don't actually have cars. They don't have the ability to do so."

NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck skewered her comment.

Sen Mark Warner Called Out In Abc Interview For Inaccurate Voter Id Claims

"Virginia has had voter ID for over a decade and had both Republicans and Democrats emerge victorious. It's an incredibly simple but important way to give voters peace of mind anytime they head to the polls," he told Fox News Digital.

Abrams has enjoyed highly favorable liberal media coverage in her career, which has included harsh criticism of Georgia's voting laws, advocacy for more progressive voting bills, and her refusal to officially concede her 2018 loss to Republican Brian Kemp. She lost more handily in 2022 in a rematch and conceded that race.

"The liberal, elitist media never fact-check these deranged assertions cloaked in historical references. If asking for an ID that must be scanned and recited to the poll worker is authoritarianism, then America stopped being a free country multiple lifetimes ago," Houck said.

Abrams' close loss to Kemp in 2018 was considered a major boon toward Georgia becoming a swing state that merited national Democratic investment.

Harris, who lost the 2024 presidential election, is considered a possible Democratic contender again in 2028. While Joe Biden won Georgia with her on the ticket in 2020 — ending a long Democratic presidential losing streak in the state — Harris lost Georgia to Donald Trump in 2024.

title: A jet engine fan blade cut into a plane and caused a passenger to be partially sucked out of a window, the NTSB says
description: A jet engine fan blade on a Boeing 737 broke free and slammed into the side of the passenger cabin, breaking a window and leading to a man being partially sucked outside the aircraft, the National Tra...
fullText:
A jet engine fan blade on a Boeing 737 broke free and slammed into the side of the passenger cabin, breaking a window and leading to a man being partially sucked outside the aircraft, the National Transportation Safety Board said in a preliminary report on Thursday.

The July 10 Ryanair flight to Memmingen, Germany, had taken off less than 10 minutes earlier and was forced to return to Thessaloniki in Greece for an emergency landing.

The head and shoulders of 61-year-old Ljubisa Karovic, sitting in seat 11F, were sucked out the window, causing significant injuries, his wife told Reuters. She and the flight attendant pulled him back into the plane, she said.

Seven and a half minutes after takeoff, the pilots got a warning for high engine vibrations, according to the report. Nearly two minutes later, the vibrations increased significantly and pilots "heard a loud bang" as the autopilot disengaged.

"Examination of the airplane revealed that the No. 2 engine, a CFM International model CFM56-7B26, experienced a fan blade separation that resulted in engine fragments striking the fuselage and the right horizontal stabilizer.," the report said.

The CFM-56 engine, built by a joint venture between French Safran Aircraft Engines and GE Aerospace, is one of the most widely used in aviation.

The shrapnel tore through the metal surrounding the engine, shattering the window at row 11, leaving a dent in the plane near row 8 and puncturing the body below the wing, as well as gouging and denting the tail, the NTSB said.

Evidence of fatigue cracking, the gradual fracturing of metal due to repeated stress greater than would be expected for the number of flights, was discovered on what remained of the blade that broke off, the NTSB said. Eight other blades were deformed on the leading edge.

Bird remains, which included feathers, were also recovered in the damaged engine but it was not clear when the plane last hit birds. Four suspected bird strikes were reported within the year before the incident but no damage was found at those times.

The plane's fan blades had last been inspected less than three weeks before because of a rule implemented after a similar incident. In 2018 a Southwest Airlines Boeing 737 fan blade snapped, shattering a window and sucking a woman's head and torso outside of the plane. She later died of blunt force trauma.

With the Ryanair flight, the 18-year-old Boeing 737-8AS was flying at about 16,000 feet in Greek air space when the window blew out.

The Hellenic Air and Rail Safety Investigation Authority asked the NTSB to lead the inquiry, as permitted under international rules. Greece will participate as an "accredited representative," according to the NTSB.

The NTSB report, which cited the fatigue cracking and said the passenger was "partially lodged in a damaged cabin window" and "other passengers… managed to pull the injured passenger back into the cabin" runs contrary to claims made by Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary in a July earnings call.

"Some of the more salacious reports that one passenger was halfway out the window, head out the window. Nobody was out any window," O'Leary said. "Initial indication would suggest that it looks like a foreign object damage to the engine on takeoff out of Thessaloniki."

The NTSB faulted him for commenting on the investigation while it remains open in a letter from Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy.

"The NTSB is currently investigating that accident and therefore, accredited representatives and their technical advisers are prohibited from making any comments regarding the potential cause of the event or otherwise conveying potential investigative information," Homendy said in the letter. "Mr. O'Leary's public statements violate (international rules) as they provide an opinion and analysis of the accident and suggest potential areas of interest in the ongoing investigation."

NTSB investigations typically take one to two years to complete and are concluded with a final report that determines the probable cause and any contributing factors.

CNN's Pete Muntean contributed to this report.
